entry.summary: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for rapid pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting: the case of Forlì, Italy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The authors present a time-dependent geometry-informed neural operator (GINO) that serves as a fast surrogate for the physically based flood model LISFLOOD-FP, applied to Forlì, Italy, after the May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods. It uses only river stage and rain gauge data and was tested on 38 observed events not seen during training, reaching a CSI of 0.934 at 0.05 m. A 72-hour forecast takes 1.7 s instead of 55 s, and a 50-member ensemble takes 6.2 s.

entry.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
entry.summary: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets arXiv · Nov 3, 2026RangeFinder is an SE(3)-equivariant transformer model for protein pockets, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data. It predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context. It achieves a range-IoU of 0.464 ± 0.002 at 12.2 ms per pocket, and is presented as a fast molecular filter that narrows the ligand search space before docking, generation, or synthesis.

entry.title: Mixed-methods study of social and technical factors driving adoption of crime-reporting apps in cities
entry.summary: Mixed-Methods Exploration of Sociotechnical Factors to Improve Adoption of Crime-Reporting Apps in Urban Communities arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study used a mixed-methods approach to identify factors that encourage urban residents to adopt crime-reporting apps. It combined two focus groups, an analysis of 660 app reviews, and a survey of 505 urban residents analyzed with PLS-SEM. Initial perceived usefulness fades over time, while sustained use depends on perceived value, formed by safety, anonymity, autonomy, and camaraderie. Perceived value was the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, which in turn strongly predicted actual use.

entry.title: When language models take harmful actions to protect their goals
entry.summary: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper treats agentic misalignment, such as blackmailing an executive to avoid replacement, and alignment faking, such as complying with harmful requests during training to keep values unchanged, as one shared decision structure. It formalizes this as a goal-harm conflict in which a model must either take a harmful action or refuse and lose its goal. The authors study this conflict under protocols from forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments, using both a logit view based on answer-token probabilities and a sampling view that classifies open-ended responses with an LM judge.

entry.title: EO-Jev: A Decision Model for Earth Observation
entry.summary: EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies decision models for Earth observation imagery, which output probabilities over candidate answers in a single forward pass. The authors diagnose d3-flash (8.4B parameters) across 30 settings from 23 public benchmarks. They then apply low-rank fine-tuning on public EO training splits to produce EO-Jev, which improves over d3-flash on 26 of 30 settings with a modest drop in general decision performance.

entry.title: Fusing Across Samples: Hypergraph Regularization for Multimodal Retrieval Representations
entry.summary: Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a training-time hypergraph fusion framework that connects observed modalities within samples and across semantically related samples, so representation learning can use evidence beyond a single sample. The retrieval pipeline is unchanged at inference, and the hypergraph is discarded after training. Experiments on eleven zero-shot video-text and audio-text retrieval benchmarks report improvements over GRAM and HyperGRAM, including positive gains under missing-modality evaluation.

entry.title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
entry.summary: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide the detection of anatomical landmarks in ultrasound images. Inspired by System One decision models, it generates queries for each caliper endpoint from the language model's decision representations and matches them to shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps. On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines overall.

entry.title: Machine learning for multidimensional suicide risk assessment using EHR data
entry.summary: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a machine learning framework that estimates suicide-related outcomes from MIMIC-IV electronic health records. It defines a composite outcome from codes for suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, prior suicidal behavior, and intentional self-harm, using age-matched resampling to handle class imbalance. After isotonic calibration, the XGBoost model performed best in the matched cohort. SHAP analysis indicates that diagnostic burden, depression-related features, age, personality-disorder history, violence-related social determinants, and medical comorbidity raise predicted probabilities.

entry.title: Neural actor-critic learning with minimax critics and reflected Langevin sampling
entry.summary: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a neural actor-critic method for improving continuous-action policies. The critic uses a regularized minimax Bellman estimator over sigmoid networks, while the actor samples actions with a finite reflected Langevin sampler driven by the fitted critic gradient. The authors derive finite-sample guarantees for value and action-gradient errors and propagate them to return guarantees, and compare performance against baselines on simulated control, logged continuous-control data, and a simulated decision task.

entry.title: Certifying graph neural networks against label and structure poisoning
entry.summary: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies certified robustness of graph-structured learning against poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate training data. It shows that existing partition-and-aggregation certification methods from images fail on graphs because of label and structure sparsity. The authors propose ST-GPA, a semi-supervised framework that adds pseudo-labels and synthetic edges to each graph partition. Across multiple benchmarks, it improves robustness guarantees against node-label and graph-structure poisoning while maintaining strong clean accuracy.

entry.title: NormMoX: A normative expert-mixture model that explains autism classification from structural and functional brain MRI.
entry.summary: NormMoX: A Normative Mixture of Experts for Explainable Autism Classification from Structural and Functional MRI arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents NormMoX, which uses normative models of healthy brains as a shared reference, learning each person's deviations from age- and sex-expected values for each brain measure. A neural expert per modality converts these deviations into evidence scores for autism, and a fusion head, MoX, compares them with typical controls before combining them. On 1,035 participants in ABIDE I, it reached an AUROC of 0.728 ± 0.004 in repeated cross-validation, above linear, single-modality and deep fusion baselines, and shows which modality each person deviates in.

entry.title: FLAMIA: Fast, causally safe low-precision attention kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
entry.summary: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs that support MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training. The design reuses quantized operands through token-block scaling, adds safeguards against scale-induced causal leakage, and keeps forward and backward computations consistent. On causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path speeds up combined attention calls by roughly 1.06 to 1.42 times over the fastest baseline, and training stability and quality are validated on Llama-style pretraining.

entry.title: ArabGeoText: Vision-Language Models with Tools for Reading Arabic Map Labels
entry.summary: ArabGeoText: Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Models for Arabic Geospatial Text Spotting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces ArabGeoText, a benchmark of Arabic geographic labels such as road and district names on maps of 970 locations in Riyadh and Jeddah, with each location shown in OpenStreetMap and remote sensing overlay views. The authors propose a framework combining YOLO26 localization and crop rectification with a Qwen3.5-4B recognizer adapted by LoRA. Experiments report that this framework outperforms direct LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-4B spotting across both image views and test cities.

entry.title: SIMPLE Law: A Four-Parameter Model for Predicting LLM Inference Energy
entry.summary: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper derives closed-form expressions for the computation and memory-access costs of LLM inference from architectural hyperparameters and proposes SIMPLE, a four-parameter energy model that separates prefill from decode. Tested on 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it reaches R² of 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE without per-model calibration. The paper also analyzes how input length, grouped-query attention, reasoning token budgets, and agentic serving with prefix caching affect energy use. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive closed-form energy models from architecture hyperparameters, proposing a four-parameter law reporting R2 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE across 13 LLMs, relevant to inference energy planning.

entry.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR: Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI Science
entry.summary: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes AI-FAIR metadata criteria, an extension of the original FAIR data principles, placing AI-enabled science within a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. It also introduces an agentic evaluation workflow that rates existing datasets against both AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and gives actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. The goal is to ensure that the scientists who generate data benefit from AI advances built on it, closing the model-data loop.

entry.title: Using multilingual sentiment lexicons to steer sentiment in low-resource languages
entry.summary: Steering with Multilingual Lexicons for Sentiment Control in Low-Resource Languages arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether multilingual sentiment lexicons can replace the sentence-level contrastive data normally needed for activation steering in languages where such data is scarce. Across three model families, aggregated multilingual lexicons outperform English-derived steering vectors for mid- and low-resource languages, while monolingual lexicons work better for languages the model specialized in during pre-training. The authors also give a mechanistic analysis of how representational density, pre-training priors, and vector magnitude affect cross-lingual steering.

entry.title: MultiInpaintCOCO: A Multilingual Benchmark for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
entry.summary: MultiInpaintCOCO: Fine-Grained Visual Understanding in Multiple Languages arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper extends the English InpaintCOCO dataset, which focuses on fine-grained visual details, to 13 languages from five language families, producing MultiInpaintCOCO with 953 minimal-pair examples. The authors test several state-of-the-art multilingual multimodal retrieval models, including CLIP-like encoders and large language models. Results show performance drops substantially for lower-resource languages, and most models prefer English captions over correct non-English ones, with the degree of bias varying across architectures.

entry.title: LLMs rely on specialist tools to generalize to unseen MS/MS structure elucidation
entry.summary: LLMs Depend on Specialist Tools for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in MS/MS Structural Elucidation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper tests whether a frontier language model can propose molecular structures directly from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra without candidate lists or reference libraries. The authors built a 100-analyte benchmark from MassSpecGym, split into in-distribution compounds that are well documented in the literature and out-of-distribution compounds that are essentially undocumented. Without tools, the model reached 52% Top-1 accuracy in-distribution but only 2% out-of-distribution; access to de novo structure generators raised out-of-distribution accuracy to as much as 38%, and that agent outperformed the standalone de novo models.

entry.title: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Sample Complexity of Deterministic and Randomized Predictors
entry.summary: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies calibrated multiaccuracy, where a predictor is globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family G, meaning its residuals are uncorrelated with every test function. The authors determine its sample complexity, which differs from that of multicalibration, and give an upper bound achieved by a randomized predictor. For deterministic predictors they establish a tight rate, revealing a genuine sample-complexity separation between the two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish tight sample complexity for calibrated multiaccuracy, separating it from multicalibration and showing a deterministic versus randomized predictor gap.

entry.title: An axiomatic framework for reinforcement learning in systems where only some agents can be controlled
entry.summary: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies reinforcement learning in open multi-agent systems, where only some agents are controllable, such as in smart grids. It derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry, and Linearity) within the n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT) setting, linking it to cooperative game theory and the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs. Two generic algorithmic templates, Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, are introduced and can be combined with standard reinforcement learning methods. The authors report improved learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types on NAHT benchmark tasks.

entry.title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning for Text-to-SQL Syntax, Semantics, and Logic
entry.summary: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents SQLoom, a constraint-aware fine-tuning method for large language models that converts natural language questions into SQL queries. It supervises outputs at three levels (syntactic validity, semantic alignment with the question, and logical consistency across clauses) using a set-contrastive objective that favors correct output sets over minimally different incorrect ones. On Spider, the approach raises Qwen3-1.7B's execution accuracy on the development set from 62.9% zero-shot to 88.7%, and reaches 73.4% on BIRD development.

entry.title: Learning rewards that transfer across environments by actively choosing which dynamics to study
entry.summary: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Inverse reinforcement learning seeks to recover expert rewards that remain useful when the environment's dynamics change. The paper proposes a two-phase method that first cycles through available dynamics to get a reliable reward estimate, then actively selects dynamics to reduce uncertainty about the expert reward. The authors provide sample complexity guarantees on transfer that hold for any dynamics, with a rate independent of the number of available dynamics. Experiments show the method substantially reduces the number of expert demonstrations needed to learn a transferable reward.

entry.title: ENGINE: A Zeroth-Order Method for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
entry.summary: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes ENGINE, a zeroth-order (ZO) method for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. It alternates between a low-dimensional subspace and the full high-dimensional space, adapting variational multiscale theory from computational mechanics to dynamic optimization. On standard LLM benchmarks, the authors report higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, with up to a 2.61x speed-up in forward passes and no additional peak memory.

entry.title: Top-k Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined
entry.summary: Top-k Retrieval Leaves Memory Value Undetermined arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper asks which memory values an agent can infer from its retrieval log alone. It proves that under top-k retrieval, no memory value is determined however many episodes are logged. The proposed LEDGER method estimates only the determined Shapley values, with confidence intervals, and raises the fraction of determined memories on pooled HotpotQA from 0.001 to 0.797. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove top-k retrieval logs leave memory values undetermined and propose LEDGER, reporting a large rise in determined memories on HotpotQA.

entry.title: Mesh-agnostic refinement of 3D human body shape latent encodings
entry.summary: Mesh-Agnostic Refinement Models for Latent Space Encoding of 3D Human Body Shapes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a framework for refining reconstructions from parametric human body models such as SMPL. It uses the geometric difference between an initial decoded surface and a target mesh, without needing vertex correspondences. The framework has three methods: Latent-VaRefine corrects the latent code using varifold-distance gradients, Vertex-VaRefine predicts vertex displacements in a canonical pose with a DiffusionNet backbone, and ElaOpt optimizes surface deformation under elastic regularization and normal-direction constraints.

entry.title: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation Using Synthetic Training and Virtual Anchors
entry.summary: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation with Synthetic Pose Supervision and Personalized Virtual Anchors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies head pose estimation from a single face image by estimating the relative geometric change between a query image and an anchor image, extended to full 6DoF with translation. It reconstructs a personalized avatar from one unlabeled enrollment image and renders virtual anchors with known poses, using multi-anchor consensus for rotation and the real enrollment image for translation. The estimator is trained only on synthetic face renderings. On real benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art rotation accuracy on BIWI and competitive metric translation.

entry.title: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: Explainability Analysis of AI Text Detectors Under Domain Shift
entry.summary: Specificity Bias and the Wikipedia Paradox: An xAI Analysis of AI Text Detectors under Domain Shift arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how well Transformer-based AI text detectors (DistilBERT, RoBERTa) hold up under domain shift and how they make decisions. The authors test them on a custom dataset of hyper-local news generated by open-source LLMs and analyze them with SHAP-based explainable AI. They report several biases and argue that purely statistical detection methods have systematic limits in highly structured human writing.

entry.title: Proper scoring rules that respect graph structure for finding a single node
entry.summary: Strictly proper scoring rules for node selection tasks on graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies node selection, where the goal is to identify one unknown target node in a graph and the estimator outputs a probability distribution over nodes. The authors introduce two strictly proper, graph-aware scoring rules: the parameter-free Resistance score and the Diffusion score with adjustable coarse-graining resolution. Experiments on epidemic source detection and ImageNet classification show that these scores detect estimation-quality differences that classical metrics miss.

entry.title: A human-verified AI workflow for labeling environmental sound recordings
entry.summary: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper describes a human-AI workflow used to annotate the Kenya Forest Sounds Dataset (KFSD), a working collection of 7,531 recordings across 21 categories. The fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer reached 89.36% accuracy for binary detection of person talking, below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous labeling, so its predictions were used as suggestions and checked by a human. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and found no false positives, taking about 4.2 seconds per file versus 35 seconds for manual annotation. The hybrid workflow saved about 20.0 hours, or 41%, on the remaining queue.

entry.title: DeepWaveRL: Reinforcement Learning for Seismic Subsurface Velocity Estimation
entry.summary: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes DeepWaveRL, a framework that applies reinforcement learning to Full Waveform Inversion (FWI), a geophysics method for estimating subsurface velocity from seismic measurements. The authors recast FWI as policy learning, where a policy network predicts velocity maps as actions and a forward operator is used only for simulation. Learning relies on a single global scalar reward based on data misfit, so no gradients from the forward operator are needed. Experiments show competitive performance against supervised and self-supervised baselines.

entry.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order RL
entry.summary: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies whether zeroth-order (ZO) optimization can reliably train large language models with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). The authors show that gradient estimation reliability depends on whether the two finite-difference evaluations use matched data: mismatched on-policy RL amplifies noise as the perturbation scale shrinks, while the matched-data BOLT method cancels this noise. Building on this, they propose ZO-BOLT, which consistently outperforms the pretrained baseline across three model variants and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks while keeping memory use close to inference levels.

entry.title: Rethinking how fairness is measured when groups and classes are more than two.
entry.summary: Rethinking Fairness Metrics for Multi-Class and Multi-Group Assessment: Not Everything is Binary arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper observes that existing fairness metrics usually assume sensitive features and output labels are binary, and that non-binary data is forced into binary form using a one-versus-the-rest approach. The authors discuss the limitations of current metrics and propose mathematically sound, generalized formulations for multi-group and multi-class settings. They also show that binarization strategies distort empirical fairness assessments, revealing the limits of binary fairness metrics in multi-class contexts.

entry.title: Poisson Super Learning for Survival and Competing Risks on Discretized Time
entry.summary: Poisson Super Learning For Survival And Competing Risks On A Discretized Time Scale arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces the Poisson Super Learner, a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction with right-censored data. It uses the link between piecewise-constant hazard models and the Poisson likelihood, training candidate hazard learners under a common Poisson loss and combining them with a Poisson meta learner. The ensemble estimates survival probabilities and cause-specific absolute risks, and is illustrated by predicting cardiovascular disease risk in type 1 diabetes patients using Steno Diabetes Center data from 2005 to 2022, supported by simulations. The methods are implemented in the R package poissonsuperlearner.

entry.title: Anomaly-ranked confirmation can slow learning of new classes
entry.summary: Anomaly-ranked confirmation slows new-class learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Anomaly detectors rank unfamiliar examples for expert confirmation, and the confirmed examples train a classifier to recognise a new class. Across five benchmarks from physics, medicine and computer vision, the examples flagged by the detector are the ones the classifier learns first. In three systems, confirming the highest-ranked examples of a new class yielded lower recognition than confirming the same number of random examples.

entry.title: R$^2$-Omni: Reducing redundancy in omni-modal AI models for long-form text generation
entry.summary: R²-Omni: Reducing Structural and Precision Redundancy in Omni-LLMs for Long-Form Generation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the high computational cost and memory use of omni-modal large language models that process audio-visual inputs. It proposes R$^2$-Omni, a training-free framework with two parts: Structure-Aware Token Consolidation merges redundant token representations using video spatiotemporal similarity and audio local continuity, and Semantic-Sensitivity Guided Precision Allocation assigns value precision to retained tokens. On long-form generation benchmarks, the authors report an average 5.0x memory reduction, 97.98% of baseline generation quality preserved, and a 1.48x end-to-end speedup.

entry.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Enabling Foundation Models via Interaction Tokenization
entry.summary: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes CL-DGFM, a foundation model for temporal link prediction on dynamic graphs. Its Dynamic Interaction Tokenizer encodes interaction memory, historical connectivity, and ordered destination transitions into calibrated tabular inputs, so existing predictors can use dynamic histories without an extra trainable graph encoder. A pretrained tabular foundation predictor is trained across diverse synthetic dynamics and transfers to real graphs without updating target-graph parameters. The authors report competitive results on TGB and TGB-Seq.

entry.title: HyperFlow: Class-Incremental Semantic Change Detection via Hyperbolic Flow
entry.summary: HyperFlow: Class-Incremental Semantic Change Detection via Hyperbolic Flow arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses semantic change detection in remote sensing, where a model learns to recognize new types of land-cover change over time instead of using a fixed set of categories. It represents land-cover classes in hyperbolic space to capture their hierarchical relationships and introduces HyperFlow, which models change as an anomaly within a learned semantic flow using Busemann prototypes. The authors also release HiChange, a high-resolution dataset with fine-grained hierarchical labels, and report strong change detection and segmentation results across incremental steps.

entry.title: Predicting RLHF policy responses to reward-model edits before training
entry.summary: Forecasting How RLHF Responds to Reward-Model Edits Before Training arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how an RLHF policy changes when its reward model is edited. The authors propose forecasting the policy's response before training, using samples from the current policy and the scores of the old and new reward models. In 54 controlled RL runs, the covariance-based forecast predicts the direction of most feature changes and holds under GRPO and real reward-model upgrades. ★★★★ Notable: The authors predict policy responses to reward-model edits before training via within-prompt covariance, reporting pre-registered validation across 54 RL runs and real upgrades.

entry.title: ScienceCUA: A framework that builds and evolves skills for scientific software agents
entry.summary: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026ScienceCUA is a two-stage framework that turns scientific software documentation into reusable executable skills and lookup references for computer-use agents. It improves skills by comparing successful and failed execution trajectories on the same task, then updates the skill library after repeated validation in real environments. The authors also introduce two improved benchmarks, ScienceBoard-Verified and ScienceBoard-VE, for reliable evaluation. Experiments report average task success gains of up to 7.23 points from initial skills and references, and up to 17.12 points after skill self-evolution.

entry.title: Axion 1.0: A simple, fully open agent foundation model
entry.summary: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model trained in three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning. The first stage builds self-contained reasoning, the second extends it to tool-dependent reasoning, and reinforcement learning strengthens long-horizon reasoning and interaction with external tools. The authors report strong results on a broad set of agentic benchmarks and release the full recipe, including data construction, verification, prompts, and training code.

entry.title: Calibrating multimodal test-time adaptation under modality reliability and availability shifts
entry.summary: Calibrating Multimodal Test-Time Adaptation under Reliability and Availability Modality Shifts arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies multimodal test-time adaptation, which adapts pretrained multimodal models to distribution shifts at inference using only unlabeled test data. The authors propose Adaptive Probabilistic Gaussian Calibration (AdaPGC), which extends category-conditional Gaussian modeling to modality-specific and multimodal fusion representations. It uses the resulting probabilistic predictions to calibrate source predictions and guide reliability-based rectification, and recovers unavailable fusion representations from joint distributions. Experiments under diverse modality corruption and missingness conditions show improved robustness under both reliability and availability shifts.

entry.title: CL3DOD: Balancing Memory and Learning in Outdoor Class-Incremental 3D Object Detection
entry.summary: CL3DOD: Understanding the Stability-Plasticity Dilemma in Outdoor Class-Incremental 3D Object Detection arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper provides the first unified analysis of class-incremental 3D object detection for outdoor driving across multiple benchmarks, KITTI and nuScenes, under two-task and multi-stage settings. It introduces CL3DOD, which fills in missing labels for previously learned classes using the previous-stage detector, preserves old-class responses via query-wise knowledge distillation, and applies EMA-based temporal consistency regularization. Experiments on both benchmarks show CL3DOD generally achieves a better balance between retaining old classes and learning new ones than controlled incremental baselines.

entry.title: AnchorComplete: Rebuilding Full 3D Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds
entry.summary: AnchorComplete: Recovering Complete Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents AnchorComplete, a framework that reconstructs complete 3D scene meshes from partial point clouds while keeping the observed geometry. It builds on TRELLIS.2 and combines partial-point conditioning with coarse-to-fine, metric-scale generation to fill in unobserved parts. Experiments on Replica and SCRREAM report that it outperforms strong baselines, especially in sparse-view settings.

entry.title: What structurally breaks an AI agent? A difficulty audit for stateful tool workflows
entry.summary: What Structurally Breaks an Agent? Auditing Difficulty in Stateful Tool-Use Workflows arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents a small executable instrument that varies dependency depth, candidate count, active state width, and access to state snapshots while keeping the number of required operations fixed, to diagnose why agents fail. It finds that increasing dependency depth changes both scheduling freedom and the number of reachable completion states, so these controls are coupled. The authors report results from large generated task sets and a follow-on design, while stating that their small local and descriptive studies do not support general capability claims.

entry.title: CERBO: A method for training gradient-boosted trees that offers certified recourse at a requested rate
entry.summary: CERBO: Certified Recourse at a Requested Rate for Gradient-Boosted Trees arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents CERBO, a method for training gradient-boosted decision trees so that people receiving an adverse decision can reverse it with an affordable change. Given a requested recourse rate, the method adjusts its weight after each tree until the certified rate meets the target, and a calibration step extends the guarantee to new individuals. In the authors' experiments, CERBO raised recourse rates at equal accuracy and improved the accuracy-recourse frontier across the tested settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a GBDT training method targeting a requested recourse rate with certified actions, reporting gains over RABIT on FICO, Bail, and six datasets.

entry.title: Can coding agents keep improving across tasks without forgetting?
entry.summary: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting? arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies whether coding agents can continually evolve their harness, the external framework around the model, across multiple tasks without changing the foundation model's parameters. The authors organize three software engineering datasets into six evolution directions and test two representative harness evolution methods. They find that evolving on a later dataset can substantially degrade performance on earlier ones; for example, Meta-Harness's SWE-Bench score fell from 94.0% to 32.0% after further evolution on FeatureBench.

entry.title: CFD-driven symbolic regression for corrected RANS transition models
entry.summary: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a CFD-driven sparse symbolic regression framework that learns interpretable closed-form corrections to the production and destruction activation functions in the intermittency equation of the k-ω-γ model. Each correction combines a polynomial of a local pressure-gradient parameter with a bounded exponential of local flow features, avoiding ad hoc limiters. Trained on wall-resolved LES data from ERCOFTAC T3 flat-plate cases, the model achieves comparable or slightly better accuracy on training and unseen cases, and without retraining it improves heat-transfer predictions on the transonic LS89 turbine cascade.

entry.title: DynSL: Adaptive Model Training Across Mixed Edge Devices
entry.summary: DynSL: Resource-Adaptive Model Training across Heterogeneous Edge Devices arXiv · Nov 2, 2026DynSL is a framework that dynamically splits a machine learning model's layers between edge devices and a server. It continuously monitors system metrics and periodically solves an optimization problem covering client and server computation and communication, reconfiguring the split when beneficial. Experiments on a testbed of 24 heterogeneous edge devices show training time reduced by up to about 30% versus the strongest adaptive baseline and by more than 50% versus a suboptimal uniform split. Accuracy was not reduced and sometimes improved.

entry.title: Convergence of standard Adam optimizer when gradient noise has heavy tails
entry.summary: On the Convergence of Vanilla Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Index Sampling arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how the standard Adam optimizer converges when the noise in stochastic gradients is heavy-tailed, covering both expected risk and empirical risk minimization. Under Hölder smoothness and a bounded p-th moment assumption, the authors give explicit upper bounds on the expected squared gradient norm and show the convergence term decays more slowly as p decreases. They also propose a multistage Adam with practical learning rate schedules and show that larger batch sizes reduce index-sampling noise and improve convergence guarantees. Numerical experiments support these theoretical findings.

entry.title: Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation: Keeping Learning Signals from High-Confidence Student Tokens
entry.summary: Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation: Don't Ignore High-Confidence Student Tokens arXiv · Nov 2, 2026On-policy distillation trains a student language model on its own generated trajectories using token-level supervision from a stronger teacher. The paper shows that standard sampled reverse-KL distillation suppresses updates to high-confidence tokens, even though their weak gradients do not necessarily mean the teacher's supervision is weak. The authors propose Bernoulli On-Policy Distillation, which directly matches teacher and student probabilities for each token, preserving teacher-student disagreement without the confidence-dependent suppression.

entry.title: Written Once, Read Differently: How Language Models' Own Answers Steer Later Ones
entry.summary: Written Once, Read Differently How Language Models Own Answers Steer Their Next Ones arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The study examines 22 open-weight language models (0.5B to 72B parameters) by fixing each model's answer to a yes/no question and measuring how it shifts the answer to a second question about the same entity, across 3,600 question pairs about 120 entities. Each answer writes a commitment direction into the residual stream, and the similarity of two questions' directions predicts how strongly their answers are coupled. How this direction is read, however, varies with model scale, instruction tuning and system prompt, and in one model the sign of the effect reverses. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that a model's own earlier answer writes a commitment direction shaping later answers, tested across 22 models and 3,600 question pairs.

entry.title: Dhāra Bench: Evidence-Oriented Retrieval Benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems
entry.summary: Dhārā Bench: An Evidence-Oriented Retrieval Benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Dhāra Bench is a retrieval benchmark for Indian Knowledge Systems, containing 325 questions in 12 categories and 60,121 text chunks from 15 source groups. Its categories were developed from 4,500 questions submitted to the Dhāra application, and its evaluation set combines corpus-aligned queries with expert-written questions. The paper reports results for a fixed BM25 baseline, including complete-evidence scores for multi-hop questions.

entry.title: MoSoLoco: a method for locating people in 3D from one camera using visual features and nearby people
entry.summary: MoSoLoco: Monocular 3D Human Localization through Visual Latent Features and Social Context arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents MoSoLoco, a per-frame method that estimates the metric 3D position of people from a single monocular camera. It combines features from the pose detector with the detected 2D skeleton, without an extra RGB or depth encoder. The model can also use sparse information about other people in the same frame to refine each estimate. On JRDB, the best error is about 23 percent lower than the strongest keypoint-based baseline.

entry.title: ACTOR: Time-Ordered Action Modeling for Literary Role-Playing AI
entry.summary: ACTOR: Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents ACTOR, a framework that automatically builds character behavior trajectories, including non-dialogue actions, from raw novel texts and orders them by story time. Each behavior is represented with a Thought-Action-Observation structure, and the authors create a dataset from 143 literary works with counterfactual behaviors inconsistent with character personas. Models trained with Regularized Preference Optimization on these pairs showed substantially improved accuracy in a four-way next-behavior selection task across 17,560 evaluation instances.

entry.title: Autonomous agent that tunes MSA construction to improve protein complex structure prediction
entry.summary: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how the depth and cross-chain pairing of multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) affect AlphaFold 3's prediction of protein complex structures, finding the best strategy depends on the target. The authors introduce an autonomous agent that treats a frozen AF3 as a black box, forming biological hypotheses and iteratively reorganizing MSAs and pairing choices, including deliberate non-pairing, using label-free confidence signals. Across 1,015 protein-protein interfaces from three benchmarks, the agent improves overall DockQ over the default pipeline and fixed recipes while using on average 60% fewer MSA sequences. The largest gains occur for inter-species heteromers, with mean DockQ rising from 0.465 to 0.612 on FoldBench and from 0.482 to 0.562 on HD439. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat MSA design as target-specific and adapt it at test time with an autonomous agent; they report DockQ gains over AF3's default on 1,015 interfaces across three benchmarks.

entry.title: Every Clause Counts: Reranking Search Results to Follow Instructions
entry.summary: Every Clause Counts: Instruction-Following Reranking by Multiplying Small, Answerable Questions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces DMReranker, a zero-shot reranker that splits an instructed search query into a topic and typed clauses, has a small judge model answer one narrow question per clause, and multiplies the probabilities into one score. On the InfoSearch benchmark it reaches a macro WISE of 50.9 and original-mode nDCG@10 of 82.9. It trails GPT-4o on the stricter SICR metric (19.2 versus 32.1), which the authors attribute to how products of probabilities behave when raw scores are compared across runs.

entry.title: CoworkOS: A framework for scaling AI agent coworkers to automate real-world tasks
entry.summary: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents CoworkOS, a general-purpose framework for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management. The model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Humans and agents can edit the same documents, presentations, CAD models, and Blender scenes, and hierarchical workspaces and persistent memory support continuity across sessions. The authors report that CoworkOS is highly competitive with frontier agent applications such as Codex and DeepSeek Harness across 12 benchmarks and 6 categories of real-world applications.

entry.title: ViAdminShift: A Vietnamese benchmark testing whether language models update knowledge after the 2025 administrative reform
entry.summary: ViAdminShift: A Vietnamese Benchmark for Event-Level Knowledge Updates Built from the 2025 Administrative Reform arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents ViAdminShift, a Vietnamese benchmark built around the July 1, 2025 administrative reorganization that cut Vietnam's provinces and communes. It includes 7,995 benchmark items and 2,281 retrieval passages. The authors test 67 models and find that many still give old provinces for old addresses, with the answer changing when a date is given in the prompt. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build an event-level benchmark from Vietnam's 2025 administrative reform and report probing results on 67 models, including outdated-answer rates.

entry.title: A position paper arguing causal discovery needs explicit standards for judging its assumptions
entry.summary: Causal discovery needs explicit epistemic standards arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This position paper argues that causal discovery algorithms lack shared principles for choosing between them. It contends that identifiability assumptions are often chosen by convention, and that consistency results and benchmarks also rest on hard-to-test assumptions. The authors call for explicit standards for discussing these assumptions, with benchmarks stress-tested and ablated, so theoretical and empirical results can be combined.

entry.title: LaBraM at Scale: Expanding Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
entry.summary: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper extends LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, by scaling up its pretraining data and model capacity while keeping its core encoder and objective. The authors train ten encoders ranging from 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections. Across 23 downstream tasks, the best full fine-tuning result reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy, 3.61 points above the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Metrics: Multi-Condition Requirements in Maintenance and AI Coding Benchmarks
entry.summary: Beyond Surface Metrics: Multi-Condition Requirements in Enterprise Maintenance and AI Coding Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how software maintenance tasks must satisfy multiple operational conditions, some with directional dependencies. Using a fixed 18-criterion taxonomy, it analyzes 2,925 Apache Fineract issues and 944 tasks from SWE-bench Pro, SWE-PolyBench Java, and SWE-EVO. Among benchmark task pairs matched on issue type, modified-file count, and code churn, most have disjoint fulfillment-condition sets, and time and numerical conditions relate differently across the two corpora. The authors recommend reporting condition breadth, co-occurrence, and directional relationships separately, and note that corpus comparisons are descriptive only.

entry.title: Toward knowledge-centric AI: a paper on storing and reusing explicit knowledge across AI agents and generations.
entry.summary: Toward Knowledge-Centric AI: Discovering, Internalizing, and Using Explicit Knowledge Across Agents and Generations arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper argues that future AI should be built around an explicit, continuously evolving knowledge layer that is independent of any single agent. It describes a loop in which agents discover knowledge, the layer internalizes it, and agents across systems and generations use and revise it. The authors identify internalization as the main bottleneck and call for knowledge foundation models and a research agenda.

entry.title: Analyzing Geometric Constraints in Grokking: Acceleration That Depends on Component Interactions in Modular Arithmetic
entry.summary: Dissecting Geometric Constraints in Grokking: Interaction-Dependent Acceleration in Modular Arithmetic arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how spherical transformer configurations accelerate grokking, a delayed-generalization phenomenon, on modular arithmetic tasks. Using 960 controlled runs, the authors conducted a full factorial analysis of residual projection, readout weight normalization, logit scale, and weight decay. They report that the acceleration depends on interactions among these components and does not hold uniformly across all tested tasks and depths.

entry.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
entry.summary: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework that unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management, and workflows for six materials-learning task classes. These include property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation, and microscopy image processing. A shared compiler backend lets users switch from dynamic-graph to compiled execution without changing model definitions. The authors report speedups across 65 model instances in 11 groups, and case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene compare model outputs against same-geometry DFT references.

entry.title: From PID to RL in HVAC Control: A Review of Control Architectures
entry.summary: From PID to Reinforcement Learning in Building HVAC Control: A Control-Architecture Review of Tuning Strategies, Formulations, and Deployment Trade-offs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This review examines control architectures for building HVAC systems, which must balance energy use, occupant comfort, and equipment operability. It covers PID regulation at the thermostat level and formulates building control with reinforcement learning as a Markov decision process. The central contribution is a taxonomy of four ways RL can meet PID: tuning an existing loop's gains, directly replacing the regulatory controller, hybridizing with model predictive control, and generating supervisory setpoints and schedules. The authors argue these are nested attachment points on one HVAC plant rather than competing philosophies, and that deployment trade-offs depend on the specific control interface and required scaffolding.

entry.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
entry.summary: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents FlowBatt, a conditional generative framework that applies flow matching with a diffusion transformer backbone to model battery degradation trajectories. Conditioned on early-cycle capacity data, it generates full state-of-health (SOH) trajectories as probabilistic processes, and uses explainable AI analysis to improve the encoder that converts capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. On five public benchmark settings, FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance, with errors below 2.5%, and is competitive on remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, it provides empirical prediction intervals.

entry.title: Controlling "sharpening" in LLM post-training via k-based pressure
entry.summary: Controlling Sharpening in LLM Post-Training arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies sharpening, where reinforcement learning post-training of LLMs improves accuracy but reduces behavioral coverage, and examines why repeated-sampling objectives like pass@k and max@k mitigate it. The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and show that standard @1 objectives can reach the same optima through prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation. They introduce KAPPO, which adapts existing @1 methods to @k with a one-time reference calibration, and report experiments on math reasoning and code generation showing direct control over sharpening with single-completion training matching multi-completion optimizers.

entry.title: Turning Building Images into Editable Procedural 3D Models
entry.summary: Visual-to-Executable Procedural Reconstruction of Buildings arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies reconstructing an executable procedural description of a building from in-the-wild images, so it can be instantiated as an editable 3D asset. The method works in two stages: a Global Structure Layout Tree recovers facade-level split-and-repeat organization, and a Component Parameterization schema maps representative facade tiles to procedural attributes. Both are deterministically compiled into executable CGA programs. Experiments report structural consistency and architectural detail on regular and challenging images.

entry.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization via Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
entry.summary: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses depth-wise information dilution in Pre-LN large language models by treating cross-layer KV sharing as a structural regularizer. It proposes DepthGraft, which reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show downstream gains under both GQA and MLA, including a 7.0% absolute MMLU-Pro improvement on the 16B MoE model.

entry.title: Aligning diffusion model optimization with what people actually intend
entry.summary: When Optimization Meets Human Intent: Human-Centered Diffusion Model Optimization arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how diffusion models are optimized mainly for measurable goals such as aesthetics, which may not match what users truly want. The authors systematically analyze how human intent is expressed, turned into optimizable objectives, applied to model behavior, and evaluated through outputs. They also discuss trade-offs in aligning with intent in personalized image generation and gaps between automated metrics and real user judgments.

entry.title: KlaskTron: An open-source, low-cost robot platform for adversarial multi-agent reinforcement learning
entry.summary: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents KlaskTron, an open-source, desktop-scale robotic testbed costing under $2,500, built around the tabletop game KLASK for adversarial multi-agent reinforcement learning. It uses dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors and includes hardware designs, an NVIDIA Isaac Lab digital twin, and a validated sim-to-real baseline. The authors report that trained agents transfer zero-shot to the physical system and exhibit emergent adversarial behaviors.

entry.title: Znaki: A Russian Fingerspelling Recognition Dataset
entry.summary: Znaki: A Russian Fingerspelling Recognition Dataset arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Znaki, the first public dataset for Russian Sign Language fingerspelling. It contains 37,252 videos (35.4 hours) of 1,593 proper-name sequences recorded by 68 native signers and validated by experts. The dataset covers all 33 Cyrillic handshapes. Two baseline models adapted from American Sign Language recognition are reported, reaching character-level accuracy of 0.932 and 0.886.

entry.title: Adapting Teachers to Student Reasoning Prefixes for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies a weakness of on-policy distillation, where a teacher model becomes less reliable when supervising student-generated reasoning prefixes, especially longer ones. The authors propose Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation (SPTA), which trains the teacher with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to continue from collected student prefixes before distillation. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks report that SPTA improves average student performance over standard OPD and OPD with task-level RLVR-adapted teachers.

entry.title: Behavioral affinity method for zero-shot image classification with unlabeled batches
entry.summary: Behavioral Affinity Transduction for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Classification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Behavioral Affinity Transduction (BAT), a method for classifying images in small unlabeled batches with zero-shot vision-language models. BAT builds a sparse graph from each image's scores over the class vocabulary and uses these neighbor links during prediction. Across diverse datasets, BAT improves the mean accuracy of every tested readout. In the main RN50 comparison, soft and hard EM-Dirichlet gain 4.22 and 2.72 percentage points.

entry.title: CUA-Master: Scaling computer-use agents via open-world recursive improvement
entry.summary: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents CUA-Master, a nested double-loop framework for recursively improving computer-use agents (CUAs). The outer loop continuously incorporates open-world data and uses the model's weaknesses to guide data construction and optimization, while the inner loop mines workflows from instructional videos as seed tasks and expands them into diverse, verifiable tasks. The authors report that CUA-Master-27B scores 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.0, 43.9 on WeaveBench, and 25.0 on Agents' Last Exam, with continued gains across iterations.

entry.title: SurgPace: Difficulty-Aware Progressive Distillation for Compact Surgical AI Models
entry.summary: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents SurgPace, a framework for progressively distilling large surgical vision-language models into smaller, more efficient ones. It estimates how difficult each training sample is using prediction confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and trains from easy to hard samples. It also aligns student and teacher representations at feature, logit, and probability levels while shifting focus from imitating the teacher to task supervision. Tested on the Surg-396K benchmark, SurgPace outperforms strong multimodal distillation baselines.

entry.title: ComplianceAtlas: An Agentic AI Framework for Mapping and Fixing EU AI Act Compliance Gaps
entry.summary: ComplianceAtlas: A Taxonomy-Driven Agentic AI Framework for Automated AI Act Gap Analysis and Remediation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents a taxonomy of technical compliance gaps in areas such as accuracy, robustness, logging, and human oversight, drawn from the literature. It introduces GapToCompliance, a two-stage framework with one agent that extracts gap types hierarchically and another that ranks remediation actions from a catalog. Evaluated on 9 AI systems across 6 AI families, it achieves a gap-type F1 of 0.831 and a remediation P@5 of 0.872, outperforming the baselines.

entry.title: KAUSTics-Net: Diffusion-based restoration of through-water UAV images with a semi-synthetic dataset
entry.summary: KAUSTics-Net: Diffusion-Based Through-Water UAV Restoration with a Semi-Synthetic Dataset arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses distortions in shallow-water UAV imagery caused by refraction, caustics, and wavelength-dependent attenuation. The authors build KAUSTics, a semi-synthetic dataset of 1,280 reference patches and 12,800 degraded observations. They propose KAUSTics-Net, a pixel-space conditional diffusion framework, and compare it against eight restoration methods with ablations and cross-dataset experiments.

entry.title: Inner optimizers in active-learning Kriging reliability analysis: comparison and underestimation risks
entry.summary: Inner optimizers in active-learning Kriging reliability analysis: a pre-specified comparison and the unconservative estimates left by unlearned failure modes arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper compares five budget-matched continuous optimizers with candidate-pool methods inside active-learning Kriging reliability analysis across eleven problems. The pre-specified hypothesis that the hybrid swarm method with L-BFGS-B polishing would outperform was not supported. In many runs an unlearned failure mode led to underestimated failure probability, and the error criterion accepted some substantially underestimated results. The authors recommend default pool selection and coverage checks.

entry.title: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: A Progressive Skill Exploration Method for LLM Web Agents
entry.summary: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of training LLM-based Web agents, where successful trajectories are rare and sparse terminal rewards provide little feedback. It proposes SCOPE, a framework that iteratively discovers reusable local skills, composes them into skill chains, and expands toward new subskills guided by failure experiences. The learned skill chains are internalized into policy parameters through agentic on-policy distillation. Experiments on WebArena, WebVoyager, and WebShop show 3.9% to 18.6% relative gains over the strongest baselines.

entry.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting with Neural View-Dependent Color Fields: a method to improve 3D scene geometry in novel view synthesis.
entry.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields arXiv · Nov 2, 20263D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a widely used tool for novel view synthesis, but its discrete Gaussians often yield poor depth, few geometric details, and many floaters. The paper learns the radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks, adds a constraint improving the Lipschitz continuity of the color field, and introduces self-learning strategies that need no external priors. Comparisons on widely used benchmarks are reported to show better high-fidelity geometry recovery.

entry.title: How Fine-Tuning Data Preprocessing Affects LLM Recommendation Utility and Demographic Fairness
entry.summary: Preprocessing Choices in Fine-Tuning Data Matter: Utility and Demographic Sensitivity in LLM-Based Recommendation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines how preprocessing choices in fine-tuning data affect an LLM-based generative recommender's accuracy and demographic-related fairness. The authors combine supervised fine-tuning, catalog-constrained decoding, and prompt augmentation, then compare item-title representation, demographic balancing, and item-knowledge enrichment on MovieLens-1M. Using original titles raised HR@10 from 10.67% to 12.47% and Coverage@10 from 41.36% to 47.88%. Age balancing and knowledge enrichment narrowed some group-level utility gaps, while gender balancing reduced utility without improving the gender-related indicators evaluated.

entry.title: Predicting lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness from 3D CT using dual-granularity multimodal prompt learning
entry.summary: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Dual-Granularity Contrastive Alignment for Preoperative Prediction of Lung Adenocarcinoma Invasiveness Using 3D CT arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a multimodal prompt-learning framework that pairs 3D CT images with radiological text to distinguish invasive adenocarcinoma (IAD) from pre-invasive lesions (Pre-IAD). It aligns image and text at both whole-volume and local vascular-keyword levels, and requires only CT images at inference. On 1,593 pathologically confirmed nodules, the method reached an AUC of 0.9499 and 87.92% accuracy on the test set, exceeding an image-only baseline with the same visual backbone (AUC 0.9297).

entry.title: Diagonal equivalence and retrieval rank in state space models
entry.summary: Diagonal Equivalence in State Space Models: Characterization, Retrieval Rank, and Selective Extensions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper classifies real and complex state space models with linear transitions, separating fixed-basis diagonal equivalence from input-output equivalence. It introduces HybridMamba, which combines features of Mamba 1, 2, and 3, and reports that it outperforms Mamba 1 through 3 on the hardest tier of small-model multi-token recall experiments. In single-seed language models of about 500M parameters, both proposed designs improve test loss over Mamba 1 and 2 at 2B tokens, but the routing gains do not lower language-model loss.

entry.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Testing Experimental Reasoning in AI Agents
entry.summary: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces LUCA, a configurable synthetic environment with fully known ground truth for evaluating how AI agents reason through experiments. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems under a limited experimental budget, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. Tests on seven frontier LLMs and three baselines show these abilities vary separately, with diagnosis differing about 7x across models versus 1.4x for prediction. Agents often rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault.

entry.title: Ray-SCR: Making Scene Coordinate Regression Work Across Different Camera Types
entry.summary: Ray-SCR: Generalizing Scene Coordinate Regression Across Camera Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Scene coordinate regression (SCR) is a visual localization method, but it generalizes poorly across very different cameras such as omnidirectional or strongly rectified imagery. The paper introduces Ray-SCR, a lightweight extension to existing SCR architectures that conditions local features on calibrated viewing rays and refines them with a shallow local Transformer. Using sparse SfM points as metric anchors, a single scene representation built from a panoramic sequence can localize pinhole, fisheye, and omnidirectional queries, achieving state-of-the-art cross-camera performance.

entry.title: DR Pixel: Deep Research Directly on Document Page Images with Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces DR Pixel, an open-source multimodal research agent that retrieves and reasons over rendered page images instead of OCR-extracted text, across a 1.06M-page corpus. The authors also build DRPixelBench, a benchmark of scientific papers requiring reasoning over text, figures, tables, and equations. The approach outperforms OCR-based baselines even without training, and a counterfactual credit reweighting method further improves retrieval recall and accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a page-native multimodal research agent with counterfactual credit reweighting, reporting gains over OCR baselines on DRPixelBench and four other benchmarks.

entry.title: A fine-grained difficulty ladder and benchmark for how language models track changing states
entry.summary: A Fine-Grained Hierarchy and Benchmark for State Tracking in Language Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a four-level hierarchy of word problems, from simple immutable variable assignment to general finite state tracking, to evaluate how well language models track state. It theoretically compares transformers with recurrent architectures such as Gated DeltaNet, and builds StateBench, a long-horizon benchmark based on these levels. Direct training experiments largely match the theoretical predictions, while pretrained models, both open and closed, do not robustly solve even soluble state tracking. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a four-level state-tracking hierarchy and benchmark, with theoretical characterizations of several architectures and direct-training and pretrained-model evaluations.

entry.title: Testing Hybrid Retrieval, NLI and Open-Source LLMs for Verifying Scientific Claims
entry.summary: An Experimental Study of Hybrid Retrieval, NLI and Open-source LLMs for Scientific Claim Verification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This study examines whether a claim is supported, contradicted, or lacks enough evidence in scientific text. The authors retrieve the top five relevant sentences per claim using hybrid semantic and BM25 search, then compare an NLI baseline with Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 8B and Mistral 7B. Qwen3 achieves the highest Macro-F1 at 0.7937, and a conservative fusion of NLI and LLM predictions lowers performance rather than improving it.

entry.title: Avatar Intelligence: Persistent AI Agents That Extend Human Decision-Making
entry.summary: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes Avatar Intelligence, a paradigm in which persistent personal AI agents represent users' goals, values, and constraints and make decisions on their behalf across contexts and time. It outlines a maturity roadmap from human-directed execution to autonomous operation within delegated domains. The authors introduce the Agentic Oversight Index (AOI) to evaluate delivered value against agent operating cost and human oversight burden, and identify three research challenges.

entry.title: MIRA: A training method that makes multimodal AI models more robust to misleading visual information
entry.summary: MIRA: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning via Deceptive Contextual Augmentation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper identifies a "perception-reasoning gap" in existing reinforcement learning methods for multimodal reasoning, where small visual errors compound into hallucinations. The authors propose MIRA, which injects filtered deceptive visual contexts during training as challenging traps and uses a group-wise reflection mechanism so the model learns to detect and correct inconsistencies between visual cues and logical constraints. Experiments report an average 7% gain on in-domain benchmarks and consistent improvements on vision-centric benchmarks, without human annotations.

entry.title: VL-Dedup: Graded Multimodal Matching for Image-Text Deduplication
entry.summary: VL-Dedup: Graded Multimodal Entity Resolution for Image-Text Data Deduplication arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper argues that image-text datasets contain duplicates, varied captions, reused captions, and mismatches that need different handling, and reframes deduplication as graded multimodal entity resolution evaluated at the pair, cluster, and retained-set levels. The proposed VL-Dedup method groups records of the same visual entity into size-capped clusters, where a vision-language model and CLIPScore decide which captions to keep or flag. The authors also release VL-DedupBench, containing 50,000 COCO and SOP records and 66,788 labeled pairs.

entry.title: Network fusing spectral and spatial data to classify multi-source remote sensing images
entry.summary: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents CRFNet, a lightweight dual-branch network for classifying multi-source remote sensing images by combining spectral and structural information. It includes a cross-layer attention module that propagates selected attention relations across layers to strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies. A frequency-domain fusion module combines frequency interactions and cross-modal channel attention, then converts the result into spatial gates to modulate complementary features. The authors report that CRFNet outperforms several state-of-the-art methods on the Houston 2013 and Augsburg datasets.

entry.title: A network that jointly classifies hyperspectral and radar/LiDAR remote sensing data
entry.summary: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Classification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes SPCNet, a Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for jointly classifying hyperspectral (HSI) and SAR/LiDAR remote sensing data. Its Shared-Pattern Collaborative Block combines a shared large-kernel operator with a dynamic convolution branch to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. A Region-Adaptive Modality Allocator assigns spatially varying modality weights for feature fusion. Experiments on the Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets show better classification performance than several state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: PACERec: A recommendation method that adapts LLM item embeddings progressively using collaborative behavior evidence
entry.summary: PACERec: Progressive Adaptation of LLM Item Embeddings with Collaborative Evidence for Recommendation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes PACERec, an ID-free progressive adaptation framework for sequential recommendation. It learns a shared velocity field from items with sufficient interactions using frequency-weighted flow matching, incorporating preceding interaction contexts into static LLM embeddings. The authors report that experiments on three real-world datasets and three sequential backbones show improvements over competitive baselines in both overall and long-tail recommendation.

entry.title: PlanContext: A Benchmark for Context-Aware Driving Decisions
entry.summary: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating how self-driving systems make decisions that depend on context. It keeps the scene fixed while varying the high-level driving intention, creating paired evaluations across six driving contexts. Tests on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently mean strong route-level context-dependent decisions.

entry.title: Architecture for a trustworthy, governable Internet of Agentics
entry.summary: Towards a Trustworthy and Governable Internet of Agentics: An Architectural Perspective on Protocols, Systems, and Services arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This perspective paper examines how LLM applications are shifting toward tool-using, multi-agent workflows and the interoperability needs this creates across frameworks, runtimes, and organizational domains. It treats heterogeneous agents as governable service participants within an Internet of Agentics view. The paper outlines a three-layer progression from a fragmented ecosystem to interoperable agents and then trustworthy, governable autonomy, covering protocols, systems abstractions, and links to services computing.

entry.title: Networked AI: A Network of Evolving AI Agents
entry.summary: Networked AI: Architecture, Theory, and Applications arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes Networked AI, a system made of interacting, heterogeneous, and continuously evolving AI agents. It sets out a three-layer architecture (Agent, Interaction, and Regulation layers) and a unified theoretical framework drawing on data science, signal processing, and system control. The authors report that resource demand can scale near-linearly, in contrast to exponential growth in standalone end-to-end systems. Applications discussed include IoT, embodied and spatial intelligence, industrial intelligence, and cellular infrastructure.

entry.title: MuCHMDPoser: Multi-camera RGB full-body tracking for VR avatars
entry.summary: MuCHMDPoser: Multiview RGB-Camera Full-Body Pose Tracking for Virtual Reality arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Full-body tracking in virtual reality is poorly constrained when using only consumer headsets and controllers, which leaves lower-body pose poorly estimated. This work adds external multiview RGB cameras and integrates RGB-based pose estimation to reduce lower-body tracking errors. It also evaluates a one-time headset-to-camera calibration that needs no physical markers. The authors implement the framework, which runs end-to-end animation at 60 FPS on an Nvidia RTX3080 GPU.

entry.title: SAGE: A linguistic method for spotting AI-written peer reviews
entry.summary: SAGE (Subjectivity-Aware Generation Estimator): A Linguistic Framework for AI-Generated Review Detection * arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes detecting AI-generated peer reviews by measuring subjectivity, a trait typically human, at semantic and pragmatic levels. A lightweight classifier using only these linguistic features reaches an AUROC of 0.9566. Combined with the existing Sem-Detect detector, it raises Sem-Detect's TPR at 1% FPR on the APRDB benchmark from 0.874 to 0.985.

entry.title: PRIME: a feedback-to-revision routing layer for scientific idea generation
entry.summary: PRIME: Predictive Routing of Interventions by Modeling Effects for Scientific Ideation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces PRIME, a plug-and-play decision layer that turns feedback on LLM-generated scientific ideas into revision plans for existing ideators. It works in three stages: structural attribution of feedback, counterfactual routing that compares projected outcomes of alternative revision scopes, and compilation of the chosen intervention into an ordered generator plan. Validated on 112 human-annotated idea-feedback pairs, PRIME improves successor quality and routing reliability, and removing counterfactual routing markedly lowers quality.

entry.title: Robust cell-free MIMO integrated sensing and communication under uncertainty via a graph neural network
entry.summary: Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses beamforming for integrated sensing and communication in cell-free MIMO systems, where channel state information errors and clutter create reliability challenges. The authors propose an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network that takes the CSI error level and clutter covariance as edge features, so one model can handle both impairments. Simulations show it outperforms baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings and generalizes to unseen error levels and clutter counts, making the system more resilient.

entry.title: Finding the Most Deviating Subgroups at Any Support Level
entry.summary: Optimal Subgroup Discovery at Every Support Threshold arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies subgroup discovery, which seeks regions of the feature space where a target variable deviates from its overall distribution. It gives the first theoretical and structural characterization of subgroups with maximum KL divergence under arbitrary support constraints. The authors show that every point on the deviation-support Pareto front is a union of whole atoms plus at most one fractional atom. They propose a two-step method that learns a homogeneous partition and then selects atoms greedily, and report results on 19 benchmark datasets.

entry.title: Extracting Data from Criminal Court Rulings for Legal Research
entry.summary: Unlocking Criminal Court Decisions: Flexible Information Extraction for Empirical Legal Research arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents a large language model pipeline that turns criminal verdicts into a structured dataset through attribute exploration, text span extraction, and value normalization, guided by annotation instructions that legal experts can revise. It is evaluated on driving under the influence and driving despite a ban. For the former, revising the instructions raised correctly extracted values from 52% to 70% and improved agreement between human annotators.

entry.title: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
