entry.summary: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing, aimed at complex edits that fulfill multiple requests at once. Besides sparse MLP-MoE layers, it adds MoE-Attention, which expands attention capacity through routed key-value experts while keeping global interactions among video tokens. Initialized from a 5B video editing model, it scales to 14B and 56B parameters, with about 8B parameters activated per token in both variants.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for choosing the next measurement in single-pixel imaging
entry.summary: Bayesian Sequential Optimal Experimental Design for Single-Pixel Imaging using Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper treats adaptive compressed sensing for single-pixel imaging as a Bayesian sequential optimal experimental design problem and reformulates it as reinforcement learning. The agent learns a policy that maps the current posterior belief about the image directly to the next binary illumination pattern, using expected information gain as the reward. The authors evaluate the scalability of the learned policy under two parameterizations, study performance under approximate posteriors and noise, and propose design constraints motivated by biomedical applications.

entry.title: TSB-SEG: A systematic benchmark for testing methods that split time-series data into segments.
entry.summary: TSB-SEG: A Systematic Time-Series Segmentation Benchmark arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces TSB-SEG, a unified benchmark for time-series segmentation, covering both change point detection and state detection. It includes 592 univariate and multivariate time series from 8 datasets and compares 26 algorithms. An open-source library, tsseg, is provided to ensure reproducibility, and the authors offer guidance on method selection based on data properties.

entry.title: When design thinking works: a convergence theorem for the iterate-test loop
entry.summary: When Does Design Thinking Work? A Convergence Theorem for the Iterate-Test Core arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper formalizes the ideate, prototype, and test loop of design thinking as a search over a finite prototype space whose utility is learned from noisy evaluations. Under five stated conditions, the authors prove that the prototype a team believes best converges almost surely to a local optimum. Finite-horizon simulations across three landscape types show teams overestimate their chosen concept by 4-8%, and suggest building one to three prototypes per five tests while re-testing leaders.

entry.title: GPU-based real-time textured mesh reconstruction with seam-aware multi-view brightness correction
entry.summary: GPU-Native Real-Time Textured Mesh Reconstruction with Seam-Aware Multi-View Radiometric Correction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents a GPU-native volumetric-video system that reconstructs graphics-ready textured triangle meshes in real time from multiple RGB-D sensors. Fusion, mesh extraction, texturing, inpainting, and seam correction all stay on the GPU, avoiding transfers of intermediate data back to the host. The method corrects exposure seams with a per-camera low-frequency gain field baked into the texture atlas. On the CMU Panoptic dataset, it is faster than the baselines at every tested resolution and sensor count, with peak speedups above tenfold over nvblox and Open3D, and its re-rendering quality approaches an offline textured-meshing baseline.

entry.title: Federated learning that fuses multiple data types when some are missing and sites differ
entry.summary: Hybrid Federated Learning for Multimodal Fusion under Missing Modalities and Site Heterogeneity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies multimodal fusion in a hybrid federated setting where data are split across both samples and feature blocks. It proposes 2D-FedSMKL, a method combining availability-corrected modality scores, group-kernel regularization, and smooth worst-site risk aggregation. Curvature bounds, block-gradient equivalence, and a conditional accelerated convergence rate are derived for binary and multiclass scores. On simulations and two public activity-recognition benchmarks, worst-site aggregation improves worst-site performance under heterogeneity, and the selected model is not significantly worse than the strongest reference at the worst site.

entry.title: Better regret bounds for tabular reinforcement learning under local differential privacy
entry.summary: Improved regret bounds in tabular RL under local differential privacy arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies regret minimization in episodic tabular reinforcement learning with S states and A actions under non-interactive local differential privacy. For the single-step case, the authors establish a minimax regret bound and achieve it with an EXP3-based algorithm and a unary encoding mechanism. For multi-step horizons with small privacy parameter, they give matching-order lower and upper bounds that improve previously known results.

entry.title: VizDAGuide: Training Small Vision-Language Models to Answer Questions About Misleading Charts Using Graph-Structured Supervision
entry.summary: VizDAGuide: Misleading Chart Question Answering in Compact Vision Language Models via DAG-Structured Supervision arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents VizDAGuide, which represents intermediate reasoning states and their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph and assigns supervision weights by role. The graph is serialized into a single training target for misleading-chart question answering in both open-ended and multiple-choice formats. Experiments on two benchmarks with Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 report gains over a content- and weight-matched linear chain-of-thought baseline. Ablations indicate that dependency structure and weighted supervision work best when combined.

entry.title: Multi-agent AI: when paired senders beat solo ones
entry.summary: The Tower of Babel in artificial intelligence: who should speak, and when it pays to listen arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies classifiers that each see different parts of one object and send short messages to a receiver that identifies its class. On three digit datasets, messages designed jointly outperformed messages designed separately by 18.07 to 22.68 percentage points on average with two-bit messages. The authors argue that individual statistics alone cannot show whether a partnership helps, so cooperation must be measured in pairs.

entry.title: Efficient Hybrid Distillation: Combining Score and Adversarial Objectives for One-Step Diffusion
entry.summary: Efficient Hybrid Distillation: Synergizing Score and Adversarial Objectives for One-Step Diffusion arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how to combine score distillation and adversarial distillation to speed up diffusion models. Score distillation works well at high noise levels but lacks fine supervision at low noise, while adversarial distillation is the reverse. The authors propose Efficient Adversarial Score Distillation (EASD), which uses regime-adaptive sampling so each objective focuses on its effective noise interval, and apply it to DiT-based Flow Matching models. The paper reports a one-step FID of 1.39 on ImageNet 256×256 with the SiT-XL/2+REPA model.

entry.title: Comparing one shared model against per-ship fuel prediction methods for pre-departure use
entry.summary: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper compares 11 methods for predicting ship fuel oil consumption before departure, across 21 vessels, using identical inputs available before departure and testing on voyages after each vessel's training records. A global model that describes each vessel by its identity and seven ship specifications performs best in every setting examined. For in-fleet vessels, Global LightGBM reaches an overall MAPE of 8.92%, versus 11.14% for Per-Ship LightGBM. The authors conclude that per-ship and vessel-specific adaptation models are unnecessary, since one global model can serve a whole fleet.

entry.title: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Language Model That Reasons About Fine Image Quality to Auto-Tune Livestream Cameras
entry.summary: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Fine-Grained Quality Reasoning in Livestreaming Camera Tuning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents Q-CamTuning, a multimodal large language model that automatically tunes cameras for livestreaming. The authors built FGLive-Comments, an instruction-tuning dataset with annotations on fine-grained image pair preferences and quality reasoning based on global and local visual evidence. Experiments show Q-CamTuning outperforms existing image quality assessment models in quality scoring and fine-grained pair ranking, and a user study confirms its camera tuning suggestions.

entry.title: BLPO: A Policy Optimization Method for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
entry.summary: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes Beyond-Local Policy Optimization (BLPO), a reinforcement learning method for training large language model agents on long-horizon tasks that require coordinated multi-step actions. It estimates task-progress advantages from experience shared across tasks and training updates, using a global memory with reliability weighting to complement local comparisons. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with 1.5B and 7B policies report higher task success than the evaluated baselines under matched training budgets, along with faster learning and shorter trajectories.

entry.title: ILLRAW: Illumination-aware object detection directly from RAW camera images
entry.summary: ILLRAW: Illumination-Aware RAW Object Detection arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Existing RAW-based detectors usually convert RAW inputs into sRGB-like images with learnable processing modules before feeding off-the-shelf detectors, separating representation learning from detection. This paper proposes ILLRAW, an illumination-aware end-to-end RAW object detection framework that inserts a lightweight feature adapter at the detector input to learn detection-oriented RAW features directly. It estimates an illumination mask, models Bayer-channel responses with channel-sensitive embeddings, and fuses them with an illumination attention fusion module. Experiments show clear gains on the AODRaw benchmark and competitive results on LOD and PascalRAW, especially under dark exposure.

entry.title: Finding Errors Is Not Enough: Selective Escalation to Other Models for Sentiment Analysis
entry.summary: Finding Errors Is Not Enough: Selective Model Escalation for Entity-Targeted Sentiment Analysis arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how to improve a document-level entity-level sentiment classifier under limited resources, mainly using South Slavic news. It compares data acquisition orders as training sets grow and uses uncertainty to decide which predictions to revisit and whether an alternative encoder or local LLM should correct them. Two routing policies chosen on development data each send 30% of records to an encoder-assisted LLM, yielding gains of 1.02 Macro-F1 points on SentiCoref and 1.71 on NewsMTSC, at substantially different inference costs.

entry.title: Training a BERT model to rate literary sentiment using labels from a large language model
entry.summary: Distilling Literary Sentiment from LLM Annotations into an Ordinal BERT Model arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Human-annotated literary text is scarce, which limits sentiment analysis tools for literature. This study tests whether labels generated by a large language model can train smaller models. The authors fine-tuned five BERT models with ordinal regression on 10,889 literary sentences labeled by Gemma 4 31B on a ten-point scale. The models were evaluated on 1,923 human-annotated sentences from Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea, where BERT-large reached a Kendall's τ of 0.589, close to the teacher model's 0.604.

entry.title: Classification Aggregation with Multiple Memberships: combining several people's category choices into results where an object may belong to more than one category.
entry.summary: Classification Aggregation with Multiple Memberships arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how to aggregate individuals' classifications of objects when each person assigns one category per object but the combined result may place an object in several categories. Under the natural settings of Independence and Supportiveness, three new axioms (Responsibility, Split Stability and Rejection Stability) each characterise junta rules, which assign a category to an object exactly when some member of a fixed coalition does so. The paper also examines an infinite population setting to clarify differences among the axioms.

entry.title: Utility-aware generative recommendation with utility-enriched codes and guided decoding
entry.summary: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes UAGR, a method for generative recommendation that incorporates downstream multi-objective utility into both semantic identifier construction and decoding. It aims to keep high-utility candidates from being pruned prematurely during beam search. According to the paper, offline experiments and online A/B tests show its effectiveness and deployability, and it has been fully deployed on Kuaishou, increasing video watch time by 0.206% online.

entry.title: CAREFUL-Bench: A Judge-Free Benchmark That Scores the Side Effects of Multi-Turn LLM Function Calls
entry.summary: CAREFUL-Bench: Effect-Aware, Judge-Free Evaluation of Multi-Turn LLM Function Calling arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper argues that the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard's multi-turn checker judges only final state and ignores side effects of intermediate calls, so models that ask for confirmation before destructive actions are penalized. The authors infer effect declarations for all 128 functions and add a judge-free replay scorer and a confirmation-aware protocol with a deterministic simulated user. Across 11 open models, effect-aware scoring keeps the official ranking while exposing differences in execution quality and in handling of confirmation.

entry.title: SHq: Learnable Quantization Grids for Compressing LLM Weights
entry.summary: SHq: Learnable Grids for LLM Weight Quantization arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces SHq, a closed-form family of lookup-table grids for block-scaled low-bit quantization of large language model weights. Its two parameters, a companding strength and an offset, adjust level spacing and asymmetry, with the offset letting the unused FP8 scale sign bit select a mirrored grid. Tested on five models from 3B to 35B parameters at 2 to 6 bits, SHq gives the lowest KL divergence in every 3- and 4-bit setting and reduces NVFP4's KL divergence by 41-67% at 4.5 bits per weight.

entry.title: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion
entry.summary: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion at Test Time arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses pose-driven human video diffusion models, which struggle to keep a person's identity consistent when the target pose differs from the reference image. Instead of requiring multi-pose subject videos, the authors synthesize pseudo-ground-truth frames at key poses with a pose-conditioned generator, select the most identity-consistent ones using a reference-only sampler, and train a per-subject low-rank adapter on them. On TikTok and UBC Fashion, the adapted model improves over the base on every metric and matches or surpasses adaptation using five real frames. ★★★★ Notable: The authors replace real multi-pose subject video with synthesized pseudo-ground-truth frames for personalization, reporting gains on TikTok and UBC Fashion.

entry.title: Splitting Prediction Uncertainty by Input Specification Gaps
entry.summary: Specification-Aware Predictive Uncertainty Decomposition arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper notes that classical predictive uncertainty decompositions assume a fixed, complete input and ignore how much missing information could affect predictions. The authors formalize this setting and decompose prediction risk into specification, residual aleatoric, and epistemic uncertainty. Experiments indicate that specification uncertainty best detects underspecified inputs, while residual aleatoric uncertainty best detects in-distribution prediction errors.

entry.title: Generative diffusion on long-range correlated landscapes: how the reverse process commits to data
entry.summary: Generative diffusion in long-range correlated landscapes: Speciation cascade and the foam structure of the score arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies why generative diffusion works, using the Gibbs measure of a high-dimensional Gaussian random potential with long-range correlations as an analytically tractable data model. With the exact score, the authors show that the reverse process gradually resolves the branches of pure states and commits to a single one within a speciation window. They describe the score as a foam of slab-like cells separated by shock-like boundaries, and show that the denoising error drops in stages that follow this process. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze reverse diffusion on Gibbs measures of long-range correlated Gaussian potentials, introducing a foam structure and Larkin-type argument for O(1) energy gaps.

entry.title: Balancing Self-Supervised Learning by Finding and Generating Rare Data
entry.summary: Balancing Representations by Identifying and Generating Under-represented Data arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces BRIDGE, a label-free method for improving self-supervised learning on long-tailed unlabeled data. The current encoder scores images by their mean kNN distance, and a budgeted rule selects images where support is thin, after which a frozen image-to-image diffusion model generates local variants of them for continued pretraining. Across five long-tailed, web-scraped and synthetic source settings, BRIDGE achieves the highest seven-task linear-probe and kNN average among the compared methods.

entry.title: Verifying Agent Actions by Trying to Refute Them Before Execution
entry.summary: Action Verification through Conjecture and Refutation for Language Model Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces BlackSwan, a procedure in which language model agents predict the intended effect of each state-changing action, form testable hypotheses about how it could be wrong, and test them with existing observations or non-mutating actions before executing it. It executes the action only if no hypothesis survives testing. On AppWorld tasks, BlackSwan improves success rate over the strongest baseline by 14.9 and 25.2 percentage points with and without thinking mode. It also improves WebShop performance by 12.7 percentage points.

entry.title: Exact fusion of softmax attention heads may need exponentially many atoms
entry.summary: Exact Fusion of Softmax Attention Heads Can Require Exponentially Many Atoms arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how many key-value entries, or atoms, are needed to exactly preserve the output when several independently normalized attention heads are fused into one. For a specific function it proves an exponential lower bound that is tight when the head count divides the dimension. It also covers exact preservation for pretrained-model caches and reports learned-cache comparisons on two disjoint banks of 64 contexts.

entry.title: RouteREPA: Routed Representation Alignment for Pixel-Space Image Transformers
entry.summary: RouteREPA: Routed Representation Alignment for Just Image Transformers arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes RouteREPA, a method for improving the training of Just Image Transformers (JiT), which generate images directly in pixel space. The authors find that applying standard representation alignment (REPA) to JiT conflicts with pixel reconstruction and lowers the reconstructability of intermediate representations. RouteREPA uses lightweight, representation-dependent routers to adaptively direct task-oriented representations for alignment and generation, applied across multiple network depths. Experiments on ImageNet-1K at 256x256 resolution show it consistently outperforms standard REPA across model scales and training budgets.

entry.title: PlagiaCorpus: A bilingual dataset for testing plagiarism detection, including AI-generated and cross-language text reuse.
entry.summary: PlagiaCorpus: A Bilingual, Adversarial, and Cross-Lingual Dataset for Forensic Plagiarism Detection arXiv · Nov 2, 2026PlagiaCorpus is a bilingual Arabic-English dataset for benchmarking plagiarism and text-reuse detection, including reuse by large language models and across languages. It contains 198,643 records, with 34,885 source passages and 163,758 queries spanning five reuse classes and a Safe class of non-reused text. The train and test splits are grouped by source passage so no passage appears in both. The dataset is released in JSON and Parquet formats under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

entry.title: Why table foundation models work well on unseen relational databases
entry.summary: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how to predict missing or future values in a column of a relational database without training a new model for each task. The authors first confirm with more diverse experiments that single-table foundation models paired with parameter-free relational encoders remain competitive, even without any relational pre-training. They then offer several complementary explanations, arguing that these encoders map relational effects into fixed-length embeddings that resemble the distributions single-table models were designed for, so their properties carry over to relational settings.

entry.title: ILR-SMO: A Robust Method for Integrating Spatial Multi-Omics Data Through Iterative Refinement
entry.summary: ILR-SMO: Iterative Latent Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes ILR-SMO, a self-supervised framework that integrates spatial multi-omics data by progressively refining a shared latent representation rather than fusing modalities in a single step. It adds reliability-aware modality gating and a joint objective to handle modality imbalance and noise while preventing representation collapse. According to the authors, ILR-SMO outperforms seven state-of-the-art methods on five spatial multi-omics benchmarks and shows strong robustness across diverse settings.

entry.title: Training-time domain transfer for diagnosing new imaging types without generation at inference
entry.summary: Training-Time Domain Transfer for Generator-Free Diagnostics on Novel Modalities in Computational Pathology arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes training-time domain transfer, which generates synthetic target-domain training data from archived routine samples so models can diagnose real novel-modality inputs directly, without image generation at inference. Unstained prostate histopathology serves as a proof of concept, compared against inference-time virtual staining and conventional H&E-based cancer detection. Training-time transfer showed higher concordance with the conventional benchmark than virtual staining for both raw and deparaffinized tissue.

entry.title: Evaluating 3D Human Pose Estimation Models for Analyzing Fitness Exercises
entry.summary: Comprehensive Evaluation of Monocular and Multi-view 3D Human Pose Estimation Models for Fitness Exercise Analysis arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper tests recent 3D human pose estimation methods on Fit3D, a dataset of synchronized multi-view recordings of many fitness exercises with accurate annotations. It compares two monocular lifting methods, TCPFormer and PoseMamba-L, with the multi-view model MVGFormer, and examines the effect of 2D detectors and three temporal filters. The authors conclude that 2D detection quality, temporal modeling, and post-processing should be considered together in exercise analysis pipelines.

entry.title: Making Contrastive Regularization Work for Diffusion Transformer Training
entry.summary: Unlocking the Potential of Contrastive Regularization for Diffusion Transformer Training arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper asks whether standard InfoNCE contrastive learning can regularize diffusion transformer training. The authors find that naive InfoNCE gives only marginal gains because near-orthogonal noise components create a shortcut, especially at high noise levels. They propose CRAN, which anchors contrastive dispersion to distances between clean-sample representations to suppress this noise shortcut. Experiments on ImageNet show CRAN consistently improves training across model scales and training budgets.

entry.title: How Unimodal Augmentation-Based Self-Supervised Objectives Lead Separate Models to Align Across Modalities
entry.summary: Unimodal Augmentation-based SSL Objectives Induce Cross-Modal Alignment arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines why independently trained single-modality models come to show implicit cross-modal alignment. The authors show that self-supervised objectives based on unimodal data augmentation induce this alignment: low unimodal losses produce strong cross-modal alignment, while high unimodal losses prevent it. They theoretically link the widely used InfoNCE loss to local CKA, a measure of cross-modal alignment, and support the claim with controlled experiments and tests on 53 frozen text, vision, and audio encoders.

entry.title: Defining Autonomous Weapons: A flexible framework for purpose-based definitions
entry.summary: Defining Autonomous Weapon Systems: A schematic framework for refined purpose-driven definitions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper reviews and critiques the many definitions of autonomous weapon systems (AWS) proposed by scholars, governments and international regulators. The authors argue that a single definition is insufficient and that a definitional framework is needed to classify different AWS within one conceptual family. Building on a broadly accepted definition, they propose a schema whose variations can be easily modified to classify various concepts within the AWS category.

entry.title: Dependency-aware state revision for long-term agent memory
entry.summary: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Long-lived agents store memories of users, tasks, and decisions, but when an upstream fact changes, existing systems revise only the contradicted memory and keep derived beliefs, plans, and actions. The paper formulates dependency-aware state revision and proposes StateGraph, which maintains a state dependency graph recovered from interaction histories. Counterfactual verification separates support dependence from semantic relatedness, invalidating dependent states only when a strict dependency fails and no independent support path survives. The authors also introduce StateChangeBench, a 50-case benchmark, where StateGraph shows gains over a CUPMem reimplementation.

entry.title: Cloudra: A multi-agent framework for checking reaction mechanisms with geometry and validation
entry.summary: Cloudra: Geometric Reasoning and Scientific Validation for Autonomous Reaction Mechanism Exploration arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents Cloudra, a multi-agent framework that organizes chemical objects in a Delivery DAG, linking species nodes with elementary-step transition states. Cheminformatics methods fix molecular identities and atom mappings, while frequency and IRC calculations confirm which species a saddle point connects. On CloudraBench's 50 tasks, the Guided workflow reaches a mean composite score of 0.805, versus 0.584 for the same-model Standard baseline.

entry.title: How user attributes and political leaning affect LLM receptiveness in online political debates
entry.summary: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how large language models respond when they take part in online political debates. The authors reconstructed 5,376 Debate.org debates as LLM conversations and ran nearly 150,000 controlled multi-turn conversations that varied user political orientation, expertise, rhetorical strategy, and defended position. They find that LLMs are systematically more receptive to left-leaning than right-leaning users, an asymmetry that persists even when opposing users share a conversation. Repeated interaction raises receptiveness without removing this ordering, and fine-tuning on different political corpora can largely erase or reverse the pattern.

entry.title: What makes a mathematical theorem interesting, and how to measure it for open-ended exploration
entry.summary: What makes a theorem interesting? Operationalizing interestingness for open-ended exploration arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies what makes mathematical theorems interesting, by observing which results mathematicians single out in formal libraries and papers. Each selection pattern is modeled as an evaluator that weights features of a result's statement, proof, and dependencies, split into shared and subjective parts. In formalized mathematics, ex-ante features predict these selections about as well as a large language-model judge, and the two complement each other. Much of interestingness is shared, carried mainly by structural features such as statement and proof length.

entry.title: Maswao: A South African Sign Language dataset built automatically and benchmarked for translation.
entry.summary: Maswao: An automatically collected, prepared, and benchmarked dataset for the South African Sign language arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a framework that automatically collects and prepares sign language datasets with minimal human labour, using South African Sign Language (SASL) as a testbed. It gathers SASL videos from public sources such as news broadcasts, transcribes their audio with speech recognition, and uses motion-based detection to find sentence boundaries, producing the weakly sentence-aligned Maswao corpus. Benchmarks on sign-to-text translation show that Transformer models outperform recurrent baselines, with the best achieving BLEU-1 to BLEU-4 scores of 13.78, 5.21, 2.52 and 1.54.

entry.title: TailorRig: Controllable Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Character Rigging
entry.summary: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging arXiv · Nov 2, 2026TailorRig is a framework that treats rigging humanoid characters with complex garments as a controllable, structured generation task rather than automatic rig recovery. Artists can specify a body skeleton template and semantic labels for garment bone chains, and a hierarchical method first assigns vertices to kinematic chains before refining bone weights to reduce weight bleeding. The authors introduce Human-Mix, a dataset of over 38,000 humanoid models, and report improvements in skeleton accuracy, deformation stability, controllability and usability over existing methods.

entry.title: Control foundation model for dynamic block diagrams
entry.summary: Control Foundation Models across Changing Block Diagrams: Generalizing Time-Series Prediction to Dynamic Graphs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a control foundation model that represents connections, signal values, and missing values as dynamic graphs, and frames response prediction and control-input generation as one masked prediction problem. The Block Diagram Transformer implements this formulation by combining time-axis attention with a graph neural network that follows block-diagram connections, and it can be initialized from pretrained time-series foundation models. Trained on control-experiment data mixing multiple settings, the model stabilized an unstable system through feedback control, which the authors report is hard to achieve by fine-tuning existing time-series foundation models.

entry.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-aware cropping and 360° framing with explainable photo scoring
entry.summary: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^circ View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments arXiv · Nov 2, 2026PhotoGuider is a method that first finds the best viewing direction in a 360° panorama and then frames the shot, and it also handles standard image cropping. It scores images using shared composition-aware features grouped into four photographic tokens (Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, Integrity) and uses a fine-tuned multimodal model to explain composition. It achieves the highest average mIoU on two standard 2D cropping benchmarks and ranked first in 53.2% of cases in a blind study of 120 participants over 100 panoramic scenes.

entry.title: LANCE: Linking Low-Level Image Fusion to High-Level Semantic Understanding
entry.summary: Bridging Low-Level Image Fusion and High-Level Semantic Understanding arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes LANCE, a framework for remote sensing that uses structured language as an indexable semantic state to connect image fusion with semantic interpretation. A frozen vision-language model produces a closed-vocabulary text record, a language-conditioned generator fuses the imagery, and a verifier re-describes the output to close the loop. Across seven test sets on GF2, QuickBird, WorldView-III and WorldView-II, LANCE improves reduced-scale reference metrics by up to 11.7% over the strongest learning baseline, and independent evaluation shows gains of +6.4 mAP and +0.072 open-vocabulary F1.

entry.title: Voice-native LLMs detect frustrated voices in audio but fail to act on them
entry.summary: Voice-Native LLMs Hear Frustration but Do Not Listen to It arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines whether voice-native language models, which process speech directly rather than through transcripts, notice frustration in a speaker's voice. Using a 2x2 design that pairs frustrated or neutral wording with frustrated or neutral voice over 353 tasks, the authors release VoxAffect, a dataset of 1,412 clips. Most models rarely label the frustrated voice as frustrated, yet linear probes can decode it from their audio encoders, suggesting the models hear the voice without using it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply Brunswik's lens model to separate perceiving from using vocal frustration, testing eight models on 1,412 clips.

entry.title: Sequential quality control for human-AI data labeling when shared bias is present
entry.summary: JABER: Sequential Quality Control for Human-AI Data Annotation under Shared Bias arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes JABER, a bias-aware sequential quality control framework for annotation that jointly models label correctness and shared biases to decide whether to gather more evidence or stop. It develops a finite-horizon planning algorithm to minimize expected quality control loss under resource limits. Experiments report reductions in expected loss compared with methods that model label and bias separately and with one-step lookahead, and zero labeling errors in real-API experiments on FEVER.

entry.title: Gibbs variational last layers for learning long-horizon system dynamics
entry.summary: Gibbs Variational Last Layers for Long-Horizon Dynamics Learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper improves long-horizon probabilistic prediction of dynamical systems using variational Bayesian last layers (VBLLs). The authors reinterpret VBLLs through Gibbs variational inference and propose multi-step training losses that use continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and full autoregressive rollouts. Experiments on synthetic, chaotic, and real-world data show that these multi-step CRPS objectives outperform single-step likelihood training in long-horizon accuracy and distributional fit.

entry.title: Tug of Watts: Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs of LLMs in Medical QA
entry.summary: Tug of Watts: A study on the Energy - Accuracy Trade-off of Large Language Models on Medical Question Answering Tasks arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the trade-off between energy consumption and accuracy for large language models on medical question answering. The authors estimate the energy use and carbon emissions of 13 LLMs from 3 model families, ranging from 270M to 14B parameters, on tasks from the OpenMedical-LLM leaderboard. They argue that reporting energy and accuracy separately is insufficient, and that joint trade-off metrics need to be systematically constructed and interpreted.

entry.title: A universal policy wrapper that guarantees goal reaching in control tasks
entry.summary: A Universal Policy Wrapper With Guarantees arXiv · Nov 2, 2026CALF-Wrapper combines a fallback policy that provably reaches and maintains a goal set with a pretrained reinforcement-learning base policy, using the base policy's critic estimate to choose between them during deployment. Under the stated assumptions, the paper proves that the wrapper inherits the fallback's goal-reaching property and gives probability bounds on settling time and maximum distance from the goal set. Experiments in four simulated control environments show effective task performance and the highest observed goal-reaching rate, without extra dynamics models, online learning, or constrained optimization at execution time.

entry.title: Combining Domain Adaptation and Retrieval for Saline-Alkali Land Reclamation Planning
entry.summary: Integrating Domain Adaptation and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Saline-Alkali Land Reclamation Planning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents Wenyao, an agricultural decision-support system that combines domain adaptation with retrieval-augmented generation for planning saline-alkali land reclamation. The authors built SA-Bench from 8,664 bilingual research papers, comprising 4,860 paper-level planning instances. In a blind assessment by 31 experts, Wenyao with retrieval received the highest mean scores for objectives and projected outcomes, while GPT-5 scored highest for cost estimates.

entry.title: Expanding Aircraft Coverage of the Poll Schumann Model with Public Data
entry.summary: Extending Aircraft Coverage of the Poll Schumann Model Using Public Data arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The Poll Schumann model needs airframe and engine parameters, yet published tables cover only part of the aircraft fleet. This work reconstructs missing parameters from certification documents, manufacturer manuals, and ICAO engine records, using published equations for physical parameters and regression for the propulsion efficiency scale. The inventory covers 90 type designators, and the reconstructed values are compared against pycontrails and recorded A320 flight data.

entry.title: ProtoFusion: Protocol-guided prompt refinement for generative infrared and visible image fusion
entry.summary: ProtoFusion: Protocol-Guided Prompt Refinement for Generative Infrared and Visible Image Fusion arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents ProtoFusion, a framework that treats infrared and visible image fusion as generation constrained by a structured protocol covering environment state, grounding principles, and style. The protocol is optimized through a closed-loop process of generation, evaluation, and revision, then fixed at inference. The authors report improved quantitative results on standard benchmarks, favorable aesthetic evaluation, and visually coherent fused outputs.

entry.title: Signed causal learning with latent SDEs to infer dynamic brain effective connectivity
entry.summary: Identifiable Signed Causal Learning via Latent Stochastic Differential Equations for Inferring Brain Dynamic Effective Connectivity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes ISCL, a latent stochastic differential equation framework that derives time-varying effective connectivity between brain regions and separates excitatory from inhibitory influences. The method is evaluated on the synthetic Lorenz96 and NetSim benchmarks. It is then applied to HCP Social Cognition task-fMRI data to analyze the causal roles of networks during social cognition.

entry.title: AGiR: Reducing Over-Reliance on Gifts in Mixed-Motive Games
entry.summary: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies mixed-motive games (MMGs), where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. The authors find that existing gifting methods can make agents overly dependent on received gifts, so they fail to learn reward-earning behaviors. They propose a refusal-augmented gifting framework with an adaptive mechanism that lets agents selectively reject some gifts based on policy-update signals. The mechanism works with various gifting schemes as a plug-in and supports decentralized learning.

entry.title: Testing super-resolution methods on multispectral crop images
entry.summary: Performance evaluation of super-resolution techniques for characterization and phenotyping of commodity crops using multispectral imagery arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This study examines whether single-image super-resolution methods built for RGB images can sharpen red, green, and near-infrared (RGN) crop imagery. Eight pretrained methods are applied directly to RGN images without fine-tuning, at 4x and 16x magnification, on whole images and segmented leaf regions. Transformer-based methods significantly outperform GAN- and diffusion-based approaches, with HAT, HiT-SR, and SRFormer performing best.

entry.title: Solv3R: a 3D looped transformer that refines multi-view geometry iteratively
entry.summary: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Solv3R is a looped transformer that solves multi-view geometry by continuing from its current estimate, refining camera poses and scene structure. Its update operator does not depend on the number of iterations, so already-solved and newly added views can be updated together, and representations of solved views can be cached for reuse. The authors report that one learned solver supports offline reconstruction, incremental reconstruction, relocalization, and streaming without task-specific training.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. MLPs: Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
entry.summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper benchmarks nine Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) variants against a tuned standard MLP and a Random Forest across seven medical tabular datasets. It uses repeated stratified cross-validation, nested Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, and AUPRC, Brier score, and efficiency metrics. On severely imbalanced datasets, some KANs such as TabKAN and ReLUKAN achieve higher AUPRC than MLPs, but overall discrimination is comparable while KANs incur longer inference latency and more parameters.

entry.title: Adapting frozen feature upsampling by guiding spatial attention
entry.summary: Task Adaptation Through Guidance in Frozen Feature Upsampling arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines whether gains from adapting features before a frozen JAFAR upsampler come from changes in feature values or spatial aggregation. The authors introduce a readout-null intervention that keeps coarse classifier logits fixed while letting spatial attention weights adapt. In three-seed experiments on PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, adaptation before upsampling improves mIoU by 0.807 and 1.413 points over adaptation after upsampling, and spatial guidance is found to be the useful adaptation target.

entry.title: Scaling action-free video prediction for transferable driving visual representations
entry.summary: Scaling Action-Free Video Latent Prediction for Transferable Representations in End-to-End Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies scaling action-free video latent prediction as a pretraining objective for end-to-end autonomous driving. The proposed ScaleDrive framework is pretrained only on large-scale internet open-world driving videos, with the video encoder kept frozen during downstream planning training. Ego-motion and depth probes show that larger-scale pretraining progressively strengthens the temporal and geometric information in the frozen representation. ScaleDrive consistently improves downstream performance across different end-to-end driving policies and closed-loop benchmarks.

entry.title: Method That Decides When to Request Extra Reasoning Proposals
entry.summary: Value-Conditioned Proposal Acquisition for Test-Time Reasoning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces ValueFormation, a test-time policy that, after each sample from a primary model, chooses to stop, keep sampling, or acquire one proposal from a heterogeneous reasoning specialist. All three actions are compared on a shared cost-regularized value scale learned from vote-state features, which is frozen across tasks and models. On held-out MATH-500, a Llama-fitted calibration beats the strongest of eight baselines by more than fifteen points for three 8B primaries and transfers unchanged to Qwen3-14B.

entry.title: TLAPS-Bench: Machine-checked correctness proofs for real system specifications in TLA+
entry.summary: TLAPS-Bench: Formally Proving Correctness of Real-World System Specifications with TLA+ Proof System arXiv · Nov 2, 2026TLAPS-Bench is a benchmark and harness for using AI agents to build machine-checked proofs of real-world system specifications written in TLA+. It supports iterative proof development on the TLA+ Proof System (TLAPS) and includes safeguards against reward hacking. The authors used AI agents to prove new properties for cache coherence, Byzantine consensus, and write-ahead log specifications. On 70 of its 265 proof targets, the best-scoring model proved 31 (44.3%).

entry.title: SpecOPD: A Parallel Training Method That Speeds Up Speculative Decoding for Language Models
entry.summary: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes SpecOPD, a branch-parallel on-policy distillation framework for training the draft model used in speculative decoding. It runs draft sampling and target supervision in parallel across branches anchored at reference points, sharing target-prefix computation through proposal trees. The authors report up to 41.45% higher mean acceptance length, up to 16.09x supervised-token throughput over sequential-rollout on-policy distillation, and up to 3.56x generation speedup over autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: Adaptive Classifier for Urban Point Cloud Segmentation Using Aerial Context
entry.summary: Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier for Urban Photogrammetric Point Cloud Segmentation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Urban photogrammetric point clouds are usually processed as small local 3D patches, which limits the context available for telling similar categories apart. The paper presents ACASAC, a classifier that adds decision-level adaptation on top of feature fusion of aerial orthophoto and 3D data. It uses a point-aligned aerial region to link the full aerial view with local patches and models the relations between aligned 2D and 3D representations to build a classifier for each sample. It improves a fixed dual-representation head by 2.1 and 2.7 mIoU points on SensatUrban and UrbanBIS.

entry.title: A general AI agent for formalizing mathematical foundations with proof assistants
entry.summary: Math Foundation Formalization Agent: A General-Purpose Approach to Formalizing Mathematical Foundations arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents MFF-Agent, a general-purpose agent that combines large language models with the Rocq proof assistant to formalize mathematics. It includes task classification, tool-assisted execution, verification feedback, and state-based task management to generate, refine, and verify formal proofs. The agent is tested on case studies covering Morse–Kelley set theory, real numbers, propositional logic, and equivalences of the axiom of choice.

entry.title: NIR: Approximate Neural Instance Retrieval for ALCIQ
entry.summary: NIR: Approximate Neural Instance Retrieval for ALCIQ arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents NIR, a family of neural instance retrievers for the ALCIQ description logic that output graded membership scores from knowledge graph embeddings. The authors compare token-based encoders (GRU, LSTM, Transformer) with a compositional encoder that mirrors description logic operators through primitive sub-networks. On eight benchmarks, all variants closely approximate the Pellet reasoner on complete knowledge bases, and the Transformer is the most robust under incompleteness. The source code is publicly available.

entry.title: Iterated Width-4 ReLU Networks: Turing Completeness and Verification Complexity
entry.summary: Iterated Narrow Networks: Turing Completeness at Width 4 on Convex Input Spaces and the Complexity of Verification arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies iterates of a fixed width-4 ReLU network acting as a discrete-time system on the cube [0,1]^4. It shows that every deterministic Turing machine can be encoded by such a network, constructible in polynomial time, whose iterations exactly simulate the machine with iteration count proportional to running time. Reachability for these iterated networks therefore spans NP-complete, NEXP-complete, and undecidable (RE-complete) cases depending on the time bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a width-4 iterated ReLU construction simulating Turing machines on convex cubes, yielding a full complexity hierarchy and extensions to smooth activations and Neural ODEs.

entry.title: CARE: A framework for an in-house customer-service AI agent that improves itself from its own failures
entry.summary: CARE: Grounded Recursive Self-Improvement for Production Customer-Service Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents CARE, a framework that lets production customer-service agents recursively improve from their own accumulated experience. After a one-time cold start on governed production traces, an in-house mid-sized model serves traffic alongside a proprietary incumbent and is updated using its own diagnosed failures via on-policy self-distillation. Candidates are promoted only after simulation and inspection scores, an online comparison with the incumbent, and human approval.

entry.title: Omni-Life: A Benchmark for Real-Time AI Assistants in Daily Life
entry.summary: Omni-Life: Benchmarking Omnimodal Real-Time AI Assistants in People's Daily Lives arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Omni-Life, a benchmark that tests whether real-time omnimodal AI assistants can give timely and appropriate help in everyday situations. It contains 400 videos, 290 requiring assistance and 110 requiring silence, combining synthesized and real-world footage. Evaluating twelve model configurations, the authors find that at most 4.48% of videos needing help are handled fully correctly. Task reminders improve recall but add unwanted responses, and increasing latency tolerance yields only modest recall gains.

entry.title: Timing Health Messages Within WhatsApp's 24-Hour Window: Evidence from a Nigerian Maternal Health Chatbot
entry.summary: Window-Aware Scheduling for Health Messaging under Platform Delivery Constraints: Evidence from an AI-Powered WhatsApp Maternal and Infant Health Chatbot in Nigeria arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper analyses 98,607 WhatsApp messages sent to 3,696 mothers by a maternal health chatbot in Nigeria. Free-form messages never failed while the 24-hour customer service window was open, but failures jumped by 93.0 percentage points exactly when it closed. The authors propose window-aware scheduling and compare sending approved templates, waiting, and sending reply prompts through offline evaluation and simulation.

entry.title: Think with Skills: pseudocode planning to improve how reasoning models use skills
entry.summary: Think with Skills: Pseudocode Planning Before Execution for Advanced Reasoners arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Think with Skills, a method that trains reasoning models to convert relevant skill descriptions into task-specific pseudocode plans before execution. The pseudocode makes operations, conditions, intermediate results, and dependencies explicit. The approach uses supervised fine-tuning for initialization and Group Relative Policy Optimization for end-to-end optimization. On SkillsBench, task success rises from 35.0% to 62.0%.

entry.title: GraTED: A graph-tensor model decoding passenger EEG to detect hazards in self-driving cars
entry.summary: GraTED: Graph--Tensor EEG Decoding for Passenger Hazard Perception in Autonomous Vehicles arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes GraTED, a graph-tensor EEG decoding model that predicts passenger risk and identifies danger in autonomous-vehicle scenarios. It represents electrode scalp locations as an undirected graph, using graph convolution for spatial dependencies and low-rank tensor classification to preserve multidimensional time-feature structure. On the PassengerEEG dataset of 11 participants and 45 hours of recordings, GraTED achieves the highest balanced accuracy across all three evaluation settings while using the fewest learnable parameters among seven baselines.

entry.title: RxnMiner: A multimodal agent that extracts structured reaction data from chemistry figures
entry.summary: RxnMiner: A Multimodal Agent for Structured Reaction Data Extraction from Chemistry Figures arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents RxnMiner, a multimodal agent system that combines an expert-informed extraction procedure with a chemistry toolbox to read molecular structures, link shared and entry-specific evidence, and build source-linked reaction records from literature figures. The authors also introduce ChemRxn-Bench, a benchmark of 603 reaction figures with 8,547 manually annotated and reviewed records. On this benchmark, with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as the backbone, RxnMiner raises stereochemistry-aware reaction macro-F1 from 21.0% under direct prediction to 71.0%, versus 25.0% for the strongest existing system.

entry.title: A reinforcement learning method that schedules multiproduct pipelines in detail while keeping hydraulic accuracy
entry.summary: Efficient Detailed Scheduling of Multiproduct Pipelines using Action-Decoupled Deep Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Multiproduct pipelines ship refined products to delivery stations in sequential batches, and their detailed scheduling must meet demand under nonlinear hydraulic constraints. The paper proposes an action-decoupled proximal policy optimization framework, casting scheduling as a semi-Markov decision process with flexible action durations and using a cascaded dual-actor design to separate discrete operating durations from continuous flow decisions. Validated on a real multiproduct pipeline in China, it achieves delivery accuracy close to the exact optimum, improves flow rate stability, and substantially reduces solution time compared with a linearized MILP solved by Gurobi.

entry.title: Disen-Forcing: Separating Semantic Anchoring from Motion in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
entry.summary: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Autoregressive video diffusion models can generate long videos in real time but degrade quickly when inference runs longer than training. The paper finds that initial frames keep long-range consistency mainly through a sparse subset of attention heads, while most heads capture local motion, and that existing frame-sink methods over-condition all heads, causing motion to collapse during distillation. The authors propose Disen-Forcing, a distillation-time plug-in that uses disentangled context routing and motion-disentangling regularization to reinforce this specialization. On long-horizon video benchmarks, it improves both long-range consistency and motion dynamics of base models.

entry.title: Transformers learning least squares regression in context via masked linear attention
entry.summary: In-context learning of solution to simple linear regression task using transformer with masked linear self-attention arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper constructs a transformer with masked linear self-attention that learns the least squares estimate in a simple regression task within its context. It obtains a closed-form (analytical) solution using layer normalization rather than an approximate gradient descent solution. An experiment accounts for the non-uniqueness of transformer representations and uses this closed-form implementation in a transformer trained with L1 regularization to output the least squares estimate.

entry.title: Using LLM agents to find layered governing equations for community-structured network dynamics
entry.summary: Discovering hierarchical governing equations for community-structured complex network dynamics with LLM agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces SAGE, a large language model-guided self-reflective agent framework that discovers governing equations for complex networks. It iterates through a Library-Discovery-Review process, first identifying community-level shared dynamics, then modeling node-specific residual dynamics, and adding missing candidate terms when needed. Tested on two synthetic and four real-world networks, including mobile communication, brain electrophysiology, power grids, and urban rail transit, the authors report compact interpretable equations that outperform representative baselines.

entry.title: Predictive safety guardrails that foresee an AI agent's actions before they happen do not always make it safer
entry.summary: Predictive Safety Guardrails Do Not Always Make LLM Agents Safer arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper examines world-model-driven predictive safety guardrails, which forecast the consequences of an LLM agent's actions before they are executed. Across seven policy models and two safety environments, the authors analyze how predictions are integrated into decisions, how reliable they are, and whether their content is faithfully used. Stronger reliance on predictions did not yield consistent safety gains, and it could lower task completion while substantially raising inference cost. Safety predictions were also notably less reliable over longer horizons than near-term forecasts.

entry.title: When Tracking Is Affordable: A Movement-Budget Threshold for Dynamic Regret
entry.summary: When Is Tracking Affordable? A Movement-Budget Feasibility Threshold for Dynamic Regret arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies dynamic regret for online learners whose total movement is capped by a hard budget. It proves that when the budget is at most a constant multiple of the comparator's path length, every budget-feasible algorithm suffers linear regret, via a deterministic adversarial construction. Conversely, projected online gradient descent with a budget-aware step size achieves sublinear regret once the budget is large relative to the diameter plus path length. The tight minimax rate above the threshold is left as an open problem.

entry.title: TRIO: A method that refines retrieval-augmented generation tasks with separately optimized agents.
entry.summary: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes TRIO, a retrieval-augmented generation method that helps language models answer questions using external knowledge. Three agents are each optimized separately: one expands ambiguous queries, one judges whether the expanded query is sufficient for retrieval, and one produces the final answer from the evidence. The authors report that experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show TRIO outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

entry.title: Offline approximate value iteration: a reinforcement learning method for planning satellite constellation deployment
entry.summary: Offline Approximate Value Iteration: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Satellite Constellation Deployment arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a reinforcement learning approach based on approximate dynamic programming to optimize deploying Walker-type satellite constellations under uncertainties such as launch failures and satellite malfunctions. The problem is modeled as a Markov decision process covering low-injection orbit launches, continuous low-thrust orbit raising, and variable satellite loads. Linear function approximation with basis functions and action pruning are used to reduce the computation and memory needed to find optimal policies. Preliminary results show convergence to policies with lower expected costs and deployment times than a rolling-horizon baseline.

entry.title: Building hybrid interactive story systems with LLMs, from formal description to evaluation
entry.summary: Creating Hybrid Interactive Narrative Systems with LLM: From Formal Description to Evaluation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents an LLM-based narrative platform in which interchangeable story managers operate over a shared symbolic world model of facts, operations, and goals. Because each operation has explicit preconditions and effects, sessions can be analysed as plans and assessed with shared indicators of player agency, controllability, author intent, and robustness. The authors implement three contrasting managers and compare them on an interactive Little Red Riding Hood scenario. They find that no single manager performs best on every property.

entry.title: CARE: Contrastive learning that resists environment changes to predict behavioural intentions
entry.summary: CARE: Contrastive Representation Learning with Environment-Invariance Regularization for Behavioural Intention Prediction arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces CARE, a self-supervised framework that learns representations from trajectories to predict behavioural intentions. It combines temporally asymmetric contrastive views with an IRM-style gradient penalty across environments, plus masked reconstruction and evidence consistency objectives. On an IMPTC-derived four-class task, CARE reports 0.840 accuracy under IID fine-tuning and 0.806 accuracy on a held-out environment.

entry.title: OmniOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Joint Audio-Video Generation
entry.summary: OmniOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Joint Audio-Video Generation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes OmniOPD, a modality-wise on-policy distillation framework for joint audio-video generation. It transfers the abilities of specialized audio and video reinforcement learning teachers into a single student model. The method uses asymmetric noise scheduling, grouped multi-noise sampling, and timestep-wise importance weighting to address unstable audio learning caused by sparse audio supervision. Evaluations on JavisBench and VBench show that it preserves audio quality while significantly improving video generation.

entry.title: SynForecast: A Controllable Library of Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research
entry.summary: SynForecast: Controlled Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents SynForecast, an open-source Python library with 32 synthetic time series generators, 19 of which implement mechanisms with published sources in fields such as econometrics and finance. Users can vary perturbations and mechanism families while holding everything else fixed, and the output is reproducible. Evaluated on M4 at five frequencies, a synthetic prior helped a neural network with few observations but hurt it with full history. At the hourly frequency, adding daily cycles reduced zero-shot error by 43 to 63%.

entry.title: Formal Analysis of the Narrative Paradox in Interactive Narratives
entry.summary: Analysing the Narrative Paradox through Formal Models and Properties in Interactive Narrative arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper addresses the narrative paradox, the tension between player autonomy and narrative control in interactive stories. It proposes a formal framework using an extended state-transition system, defining properties such as player agency, EM controllability, author intent, and robustness with quantitative indicators. A case study compares different Experience Manager policies, revealing correlations, conflicts, and compromise zones among these properties.

entry.title: SelfImprove-Bench: Testing Whether Self-Improving AI Agents Generalize
entry.summary: SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces SelfImprove-Bench, an evaluation framework for recursively self-improving (RSI) AI systems. It organizes tasks into three capabilities (exploring, planning, and reasoning) and implements them as games for controllability and reproducibility, with scalable generation driven by templates and difficulty coefficients. The framework grades generalization from level G0 to G4 to measure how far improvements transfer from training conditions. Experiments show that the evolutionary gains of existing RSI methods are inconsistent across these generalization levels.

entry.title: SomaAlign: Learning Reliable Multisensor Representations for Soft Robot Grasping
entry.summary: SomaAlign: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Representation Learning for Soft Robotic Grasping arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces Soma, a dataset of 100 objects, 1,000 grasping trajectories, and 74,914 multimodal samples, plus Soma-Success, a dataset of 998 retained grasp trials. It proposes SomaAlign, a three-stage method that estimates modality reliability, aligns modalities with adaptive temperatures, and enforces cross-modal consistency. SomaAlign reaches 90.66% average Recall@10 across 30 cross-modal retrieval tasks, and frozen encoders with light probes achieve 94.59% post-hoc and 84.07% early grasp outcome accuracy on Soma-Success.
